1.16: To fear the Lord is the fulness of wisdom; And she satiateth men with her fruits.
1.17: She will fill all her house with desirable things, And her garners with her produce.
1.18: The fear of the Lord is the crown of wisdom, Making peace and perfect health to flourish.
1.19: He both saw and counted her; He rained down skill and knowledge of understanding, And exalted the honor of those who hold her fast.
1.20: To fear the Lord is the root of wisdom; And her branches are length of days.
1.22: Unjust wrath can never be justified; For the sway of his wrath is his downfall.
1.23: A man that is longsuffering will bear for a season, And afterward gladness will spring up to him;
1.24: He will hide his words for a season, And the lips of many will tell forth his understanding.
1.25: A parable of knowledge is in the treasures of wisdom; But godliness is an abomination to a sinner.
1.26: If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, And the Lord will give her to you freely:
1.27: For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction; And in faith and meekness is his good pleasure.
1.28: Disobey not the fear of the Lord; And come not to him with a double heart.
1.29: Be not a hypocrite in the mouths of men; And take good heed to your lips.
1.30: Exalt not yourself, lest you fall, And bring dishonor upon your soul; And so the Lord will reveal your secrets, And will cast you down in the midst of the congregation; Because you came not to the fear of the Lord, And your heart was full of deceit.

2.1: My son, if you come to serve the Lord, Prepare your soul for temptation.
2.2: Set your heart aright, and constantly endure, And make not haste in time of calamity.
2.3: Cleave to him, and depart not, That you may be increased at your latter end.
2.4: Accept whatever is brought upon you, And be longsuffering when you passest into humiliation.
2.5: For gold is tried in the fire, And acceptable men in the furnace of humiliation.
2.6: Put your trust in him, and he will help you: Order your ways aright, and set your hope on him.
2.7: You that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy; And turn not aside, lest you fall.
2.8: You that fear the Lord, put your trust in him; And your reward will not fail.
2.9: You that fear the Lord, hope for good things, And for eternal gladness and mercy.
2.10: Look at the generations of old, and see: Who did ever put his trust in the Lord, and was ashamed? Or who did abide in his fear, and was forsaken? Or who did call upon him, and he despised him?
2.11: For the Lord is full of compassion and mercy; And he forgives sins, and saves in time of affliction.
2.12: Woe to fearful hearts, and to faint hands, And to the sinner that goes two ways!
2.13: Woe to the faint heart! for it believes not; Therefore will it not be defended.
2.14: Woe to you that have lost your patience! And what will you do when the Lord shall visit you?
2.15: They that fear the Lord will not disobey his words; And those who love him will keep his ways.
2.16: They that fear the Lord will seek his good pleasure; And those who love him will be filled with the law.
2.17: They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, And will humble their souls in his sight,
2.18: saying, We will fall into the hands of the Lord, And not into the hands of men: For as his majesty is, So also is his mercy.

3.1: Hear me your father, O my children, And do thereafter, that you may be saved.
3.2: For the Lord has given the father glory as touching the children, And has confirmed the judgement of the mother as touching the sons.
3.3: He that honors his father will make atonement for sins:
3.4: And he that gives glory to his mother is as one that lays up treasure.
3.5: Whoso honors his father will have joy of his children; And in the day of his prayer he will be heard.
3.6: He that gives glory to his father will have length of days; And he that hearkens to the Lord will bring rest to his mother,
3.7: And will do service under his parents, as to masters.
3.8: In deed and word honor your father, That a blessing may come upon you from him.
3.9: For the blessing of the father establishes the houses of children; But the curse of the mother roots out the foundations.
3.10: Glorify not yourself in the dishonor of your father; For your father’s dishonor is no glory to you.
3.11: For the glory of a man is from the honor of his father; And a mother in dishonor is a reproach to her children.
3.12: My son, help your father in his old age; And grieve him not as long as he lives.
3.13: And if he fails in understanding, have patience with him; And dishonor him not while you are in your full strength.
3.14: For the relieving of your father will not be forgotten: And instead of sins it will be added to build you up.
3.15: In the day of your affliction it will remember you; As fair weather upon ice, So will your sins also melt away.
3.16: He that forsakes his father is as a blasphemer; And he that provoketh his mother is cursed of the Lord.
3.17: My son, go on with your business in meekness; So will you be beloved of an acceptable man.
3.18: The greater you are, humble yourself the more, And you will find favor before the Lord.
3.20: For great is the potency of the Lord, And he is glorified of those who are lowly.
3.21: Seek not things that are too hard for you, And search not out things that are above your strength.
3.22: The things that have been commanded you, think thereupon; For you have no need of the things that are secret.
3.23: Be not over busy in your superfluous works: For more things are showed to you than men can understand.
3.24: For the conceit of many has led them astray; And evil surmising has caused their judgement to slip.
3.26: A stubborn heart will fare ill at the last; And he that loves danger will perish therein.
3.27: A stubborn heart will be laden with troubles; And the sinner will heap sin upon sin.
3.28: The calamity of the proud is no healing; For a plant of wickedness has taken root in him.
3.29: The heart of the prudent will understand a parable; And the ear of a listener is the desire of a wise man.
3.30: Water will quench a flaming fire; And almsgiving will make atonement for sins.
3.31: He that requites good turns is mindful of that which comes afterward; And in the time of his falling he will find a support.

4.1: My son, deprive not the poor of his living, And make not the needy eyes to wait long.
4.2: Make not a hungry soul sorrowful; Neither provoke a man in his distress.
4.3: To a heart that is provoked add not more trouble; And defer not to give to him that is in need.
4.4: Reject not a suppliant in his affliction; And turn not away your face from a poor man.
4.5: Turn not away your eye from one that asks of you, And give none occasion to a man to curse you:
4.6: For if he curse you in the bitterness of his soul, He that made him will hear his supplication.
4.7: Get yourself the love of the congregation; And to a great man bow your head.
4.8: Incline your ear to a poor man, And answer him with peaceful words in meekness.
4.9: Deliver him that is wronged from the hand of him that wrongeth him; And be not faint-hearted in giving judgement.
4.10: Be as a father to the fatherless, And instead of a husband to their mother: So will you be as a son of the Most High, And he will love you more than your mother does.
4.11: Wisdom exalts her sons, And takes hold of those who seek her.
4.12: He that loves her loves life; And those who seek to her early will be filled with gladness.
4.13: He that holds her fast will inherit glory; And where he enters, the Lord will bless.
4.14: They that do her service will minister to the Holy One; And those who love her the Lord does love.
4.15: He that gives ear to her will judge the nations; And he that gives heed to her will dwell securely.
4.16: If he trust her, he will inherit her; And his generations will have her in possession.
4.17: For at the first she will walk with him in crooked ways, And will bring fear and dread upon him, And torment him with her discipline, Until she may trust his soul, and try him by her judgements:
4.18: Then will she return again the straight way to him, And will gladden him, and reveal to him her secrets.
4.19: If he go astray, she will forsake him, And give him over to his fall.
4.20: Observe the opportunity, and beware of evil; And be not ashamed concerning your soul.
4.21: For there is a shame that brings sin; And there is a shame that is glory and grace.
4.22: Accept not the person of any against your soul; And reverence no man to your falling.
4.23: Refrain not speech, when it tendeth to safety; And hide not your wisdom for the sake of fair-seeming.
4.24: For by speech wisdom will be known; And instruction by the word of the tongue.
4.25: Speak not against the truth; And be abashed for your ignorance.
4.26: Be not ashamed to make confession of your sins; And force not the current of the river.
4.27: Lay not yourself down for a fool to tread upon; And accept not the person of one that is mighty.
4.28: Strive for the truth to death, and the Lord God will fight for you.
4.29: Be not hasty in your tongue, And in your deeds slack and remiss.
4.30: Be not as a lion in your house, Nor fanciful among your servants.
4.31: Let not your hand be stretched out to receive, and closed when you should repay.

5.1: Set not your heart upon your goods; And say not, They are sufficient for me.
5.2: Follow not your own mind and your strength, To walk in the desires of your heart;
5.3: And say not, Who will have dominion over me? For the Lord will surely take vengeance on you.
5.4: Say not, I sinned, and what happened to me? For the Lord is longsuffering.
5.5: Concerning atonement, be not without fear, To add sin upon sins:
5.6: And say not, His compassion is great; He will be pacified for the multitude of my sins: For mercy and wrath are with him, And his indignation will rest upon sinners.
5.7: Make no tarrying to turn to the Lord; And put not off from day to day: For suddenly will the wrath of the Lord come forth; And you will perish in the time of vengeance.
5.8: Set not your heart upon unrighteous gains: For you will profit nothing in the day of calamity.
5.9: Winnow not with every wind, And walk not in every path: Thus does the sinner that has a double tongue.
5.10: Be stedfast in your understanding; And let your word be one.
5.11: Be swift to hear; And with patience make your answer.
5.12: If you have understanding, answer your neighbor; And if not, let your hand be upon your mouth.
5.13: Glory and dishonor is in talk: And the tongue of a man is his fall.
5.14: Be not called a whisperer; And lie not in wait with your tongue: For upon the thief there is shame, And an evil condemnation upon him that has a double tongue.
5.15: In a great matter and in a small, be not ignorant;

6.1: And instead of a friend become not an enemy; For an evil name will inherit shame and reproach: Even so will the sinner that has a double tongue.
6.2: Exalt not yourself in the counsel of your soul; That your soul be not torn in pieces as a bull:
6.3: You will eat up your leaves, and destroy your fruits, And leave yourself as a dry tree.
6.4: A wicked soul will destroy him that has gotten it, And will make him a laughing stock to his enemies.
6.5: Sweet words will multiply a man’s friends; And a fair-speaking tongue will multiply courtesies.
6.6: Let those that are at peace with you be many; But your counselors one of a thousand.
6.7: If you would get you a friend, get him by proving, And be not in haste to trust him.
6.8: For there is a friend that is so for his own occasion; And he will not continue in the day of your affliction.
6.9: And there is a friend that turns to enmity; And he will discover strife to your reproach.
6.10: And there is a friend that is a companion at the table; And he will not continue in the day of your affliction.
6.11: And in your prosperity he will be as yourself, And will be bold over your servants:
6.12: If you shall be brought low, he will be against you, And will hide himself from your face.
6.13: Separate yourself from your enemies; And beware of your friends.
6.14: A faithful friend is a strong defence; And he that has found him has found a treasure.
6.15: There is nothing that can be taken in exchange for a faithful friend; And his excellency is beyond price.
6.16: A faithful friend is a medicine of life; And those who fear the Lord will find him.
6.17: He that fears the Lord directs his friendship aright; For as he is, so is his neighbor also.
6.18: My son, gather instruction from your youth up: And even to hoar hairs you will find wisdom.
6.19: Come to her as one that plows and sows, And wait for her good fruits; For your toil will be little in the tillage of her, And you will eat of her fruits right soon.
6.20: How exceeding harsh is she to the unlearned! And he that is without understanding will not abide in her.
6.21: As a mighty stone of trial will she rest upon him; And he will not delay to cast her from him.
6.22: For wisdom is according to her name; and she is not manifest to many.
6.23: Give ear, my son, and accept my judgement, And refuse not my counsel,
6.24: And bring your feet into her fetters, And your neck into her chain.
6.25: Put your shoulder under her, and bear her, And be not grieved with her bonds.
6.26: Come to her with all your soul, And keep her ways with your whole power.
6.27: Search, and seek, and she will be made known to you; And when you have got hold of her, let her not go.
6.28: For at the last you will find her rest; And she will be turned for you into gladness.
6.29: And her fetters will be to you for a covering of strength, And her chains for a robe of glory.
6.30: For there is a golden ornament upon her, And her bands are a riband of blue.
6.31: You shall put her on as a robe of glory, And shall array you with her as a crown of rejoicing.
6.32: My son, if you will, you shall be instructed; And if you will yield your soul, you will be prudent.
6.33: If you love to hear, you will receive; And if you incline your ear, you will be wise.
6.34: Stand you in the multitude of the elders; And whoso is wise, cleave you to him.
6.35: Be willing to listen to every godly discourse; And don’t let the proverbs of understanding escape you.
6.36: If you see a man of understanding, get you betimes to him, And let your foot wear out the steps of his doors.
6.37: Let your mind dwell upon the ordinances of the Lord, And meditate continually in his commandments: He will establish your heart, And your desire of wisdom will be given to you.

7.1: Do no evil, so will no evil overtake you.
7.2: Depart from wrong, and it will turn away from you.
7.3: My son, sow not upon the furrows of unrighteousness, And you shall not reap them sevenfold.
7.4: Seek not of the Lord preeminence, Neither of the king the seat of honor.
7.5: Justify not yourself in the presence of the Lord; And display not your wisdom before the king.
7.6: Seek not to be a judge, Lest you be not able to take away iniquities; Lest haply you fear the person of a mighty man, And lay a stumbling block in the way of your uprightness.
7.7: Sin not against the multitude of the city, And cast not yourself down in the crowd.
7.8: Bind not up sin twice; For in one sin you will not be unpunished.
7.9: Say not, He will look upon the multitude of my gifts, And when I offer to the Most High God, he will accept it.
7.10: Be not faint-hearted in your prayer; And neglect not to give alms.
7.11: Laugh not a man to scorn when he is in the bitterness of his soul; For there is one who humbles and exalts.
7.12: Devise not a lie against your brother; Neither do the like to a friend.
7.13: Love not to make any manner of lie; For the custom thereof is not for good.
7.14: Prate not in the multitude of elders; And repeat not your words in your prayer.
7.15: Hate not laborious work; Neither husbandry, which the Most High has ordained.
7.16: Number not yourself among the multitude of sinners: Remember that wrath will not wait.
7.17: Humble your soul greatly; For the punishment of the ungodly man is fire and the worm.
7.18: Change not a friend for a thing indifferent; Neither a true brother for the gold of Ophir.
7.19: Forgo not a wise and good wife; For her grace is above gold.
7.20: Entreat not evil a servant that works truly, Nor a hireling that gives you his life.
7.21: Let your soul love a wise servant; Defraud him not of liberty.
7.22: Hast you cattle? have an eye to them; And if they are profitable to you, let them stay by you.
7.23: Hast you children? correct them, And bow down their neck from their youth.
7.24: Hast you daughters? give heed to their body, And make not your face cheerful toward them.
7.25: Give your daughter in marriage, and you will have accomplished a great matter: And give her to a man of understanding.
7.26: Hast you a wife after your mind? cast her not out: But trust not yourself to one that is hateful.
7.27: Give glory to your father with your whole heart; And forget not the pangs of your mother.
7.28: Remember that of them you were born: And what will you recompense them for the things that they have done for you?
7.29: Fear the Lord with all your soul; And reverence his priests.
7.30: With all your strength love him that made you; And forsake not his ministers.
7.31: Fear the Lord, and glorify the priest; And give him his portion, even as it is commanded you; The first fruits, and the trespass offering, and the gift of the shoulders, And the sacrifice of sanctification, and the first fruits of holy things.
7.32: Also to the poor man stretch out your hand, That your blessing may be perfected.
7.33: A gift has grace in the sight of every man living; And for a dead man keep not back grace.
7.34: Be not lacking to those who weep; And mourn with those who mourn.
7.35: Be not slow to visit a sick man; For by such things you will gain love.
7.36: In all your matters remember your last end, And you will never do amiss.

8.1: Contend not with a mighty man, Lest haply you fall into his hands.
8.2: Strive not with a rich man, lest haply he overweigh you: For gold has destroyed many, And turned away the hearts of kings.
8.3: Contend not with a man that is full of tongue, And heap not wood upon his fire.
8.4: Jest not with a rude man, Lest your ancestors be dishonored.
8.5: Reproach not a man when he turns from sin: Remember that we are all worthy of punishment.
8.6: Dishonour not a man in his old age; For some of us also are waxing old.
8.7: Rejoice not over one that is dead: Remember that we die all.
8.8: Neglect not the discourse of the wise, And be conversant with their proverbs; For of them you will learn instruction, And how to minister to great men.
8.9: Miss not the discourse of the aged; For they also learned of their fathers: Because from them you will learn understanding, And to give answer in time of need.
8.10: Kindle not the coals of a sinner, Lest you be burned with the flame of his fire.
8.11: Rise not up from the presence of an insolent man, Lest he lie in wait as an ambush for your mouth.
8.12: Lend not to a man that is mightier than yourself; And if you lend, be as one that has lost.
8.13: Be not surety above your power: And if you be surety, take thought as one that will have to pay.
8.14: Go not to law with a judge; For according to his honor will they give judgement for him.
8.15: Go not in the way with a rash man, Lest he be aggrieved with you; For he will do according to his own will, And you will perish with his folly.
8.16: Fight not with a wrathful man, And travel not with him through the desert: For blood is as nothing in his sight; And where there is no help, he will overthrow you.
8.17: Take not counsel with a fool; For he will not be able to conceal the matter.
8.18: Do no secret thing before a stranger; For you know not what he will bring forth.
8.19: Open not your heart to every man; And let him not return you a favor.

9.1: Be not jealous over the wife of your bosom, And teach her not an evil lesson against yourself.
9.2: Give not your soul to a woman, That she should set her foot upon your strength.
9.3: Go not to meet a woman that playeth the harlot, Lest haply you fall into her snares.
9.4: Use not the company of a woman that is a singer, Lest haply you be caught by her attempts.
9.5: Gaze not on a maid, lest haply you be trapped in her penalties.
9.6: Give not your soul to harlots, That you lose not your inheritance.
9.7: Look not round about you in the streets of the city, Neither wander you in the solitary places thereof.
9.8: Turn away your eye from a comely woman, And gaze not on another’s beauty: By the beauty of a woman many have been led astray; And herewith love is kindled as a fire.
9.9: Sit not at all with a woman that has a husband; And revel not with her at the wine; Lest haply your soul turn away to her, And with your spirit you slide into destruction.
9.10: Forsake not an old friend; For the new is not comparable to him: As new wine, so is a new friend; If it become old, you will drink it with gladness.
9.11: Envy not the glory of a sinner; For you know not what will be his overthrow.
9.12: Delight not in the delights of the ungodly: Remember they will not go unpunished to the grave.
9.13: Keep you far from the man that has power to kill, And you will have no suspicion of the fear of death: And if you come to him, commit no fault, Lest he take away your life: Know surely that you go about in the midst of snares, And walk upon the battlements of a city.
9.14: As well as you can, guess at your neighbors; And take counsel with the wise.
9.15: Let your converse be with men of understanding; And let all your discourse be in the law of the Most High.
9.16: Let just men be the companions of your board; And let your glorying be in the fear of the Lord.
9.17: For the hand of the artificers a work will be commended: And he that rules the people will be counted wise for his speech.
9.18: A man full of tongue is dangerous in his city; And he that is headlong in his speech will be hated.

10.1: A wise judge will instruct his people; And the government of a man of understanding will be well ordered.
10.2: As is the judge of his people, so are his ministers; And as is the ruler of the city, such are all those who dwell therein.
10.3: An uninstructed king will destroy his people; And a city will be established through the understanding of the powerful.
10.4: In the hand of the Lord is the authority of the earth; And in due time he will raise up over it one that is profitable.
10.5: In the hand of the Lord is the prosperity of a man; And upon the person of the scribe will he lay his honor.
10.6: Be not angry with your neighbor for every wrong; And do nothing by works of violence.
10.7: Pride is hateful before the Lord and before men; And in the judgement of both will unrighteousness err.
10.8: Sovereignty is transferred from nation to nation, Because of iniquities, and deeds of violence, and greed of money.
10.9: Why is earth and ashes proud? Because in his life he has cast away his bowels.
10.10: It is a long disease; the physician mocketh: And he is a king today, and tomorrow he will die.
10.11: For when a man is dead, He will inherit creeping things, and beasts, and worms.
10.12: It is the beginning of pride when a man departs from the Lord; And his heart is departed from him that made him.
10.13: For the beginning of pride is sin; And he that keeps it will pour forth abomination. For this cause the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, And overthrew them utterly.
10.14: The Lord cast down the thrones of rulers, And set the meek in their stead.
10.15: The Lord plucked up the roots of nations, And planted the lowly in their stead.
10.16: The Lord overthrew the lands of nations, And destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.
10.17: He took some of them away, and destroyed them, And made their memorial to cease from the earth.
10.18: Pride has not been created for men, Nor wrathful anger for the offspring of women.
10.19: What manner of seed has honor? the seed of man. What manner of seed has honor? those who fear the Lord. What manner of seed has no honor? the seed of man. What manner of seed has no honor? those who transgress the commandments.
10.20: In the midst of kindred he that rules them has honor; And in the eyes of the Lord those who fear him.
10.22: The rich man, and the honorable, and the poor, Their glorying is the fear of the Lord.
10.23: It is not right to dishonor a poor man that has understanding; And it is not fitting to glorify a man that is a sinner.
10.24: The great man, and the judge, and the mighty man, will be glorified; And there is not one of them greater than he that fears the Lord.
10.25: Free men will minister to a wise servant; And a man that has knowledge will not murmur thereat.
10.26: Be not over wise in doing your work; And glorify not yourself in the time of your distress.
10.27: Better is he that labores, and abounds in all things, Than he that glorifieth himself, and lacketh bread.
10.28: My son, glorify your soul in meekness, And give it honor according to the worthiness thereof.
10.29: Who will justify him that sins against his own soul? And who will glorify him that dishonors his own life?
10.30: A poor man is glorified for his knowledge; And a rich man is glorified for his riches.
10.31: But he that is glorified in poverty, how much more in riches? And he that is inglorious in riches, how much more in poverty?

11.1: The wisdom of the lowly will lift up his head, And make him to sit in the midst of great men.
11.2: Commend not a man for his beauty; And abhor not a man for his outward appearance.
11.3: The bee is little among such as fly; And her fruit is the chief of sweetmeats.
11.4: Glory not in the putting on of raiment, And exalt not yourself in the day of honor; For the works of the Lord are wonderful, And his works are hidden among men.
11.5: Many kings have sat down upon the ground; And one that was never thought of has worn a diadem.
11.6: Many mighty men have been greatly disgraced; And men of renown have been delivered into other men’s hands.
11.7: Blame not before you have examined: Understand first, and then rebuke.
11.8: Answer not before you have heard; And interrupt not in the midst of speech.
11.9: Strive not in a matter that concerns you not; And where sinners judge, sit not you with them.
11.10: My son, be not busy about many matters: For if you meddle much, you will not be unpunished; And if you pursue, you will not overtake; And you will not escape by fleeing.
11.11: There is one that toileth, and labores, and makes haste, And is so much the more behind.
11.12: There is one that is sluggish, and has need of help, Lacking in strength, and that abounds in poverty; And the eyes of the Lord looked upon him for good, And he set him up from his low estate,
11.13: And lifted up his head; And many marveled at him.
11.14: Good things and evil, life and death, Poverty and riches, are from the Lord.
11.17: The gift of the Lord remains with the godly, And his good pleasure will prosper forever.
11.18: There is that waxes rich by his wariness and pinching, And this is the portion of his reward:
11.19: When he says, I have found rest, And now will I eat of my goods; Yet he knows not what time will pass, And he will leave them to others, and die.
11.20: Be stedfast in your covenant, and be conversant therein, And wax old in your work.
11.21: Marvel not at the works of a sinner; But trust the Lord, and abide in your labor: For it is an easy thing in the sight of the Lord swiftly on the sudden to make a poor man rich.
11.22: The blessing of the Lord is in the reward of the godly; And in an hour that comes swiftly he makes his blessing to flourish.
11.23: Say not, What use is there of me? And what from henceforth will my good things be?
11.24: Say not, I have sufficient, And from henceforth what harm will happen to me?
11.25: In the day of good things there is a forgetfulness of evil things; And in the day of evil things a man will not remember things that are good.
11.26: For it is an easy thing in the sight of the Lord To reward a man in the day of death according to his ways.
11.27: The affliction of an hour causes forgetfulness of delight; And in the last end of a man is the revelation of his deeds.
11.28: Call no man blessed before his death; And a man will be known in his children.
11.29: Bring not every man into your house; For many are the plots of the deceitful man.
11.30: As a decoy partridge in a cage, so is the heart of a proud man; And as one that is a spy, he looks upon your falling.
11.31: For he lies in wait to turn things that are good into evil; And in things that are praiseworthy he will lay blame.
11.32: From a spark of fire a heap of many coals is kindled; And a sinful man lies in wait for blood.
11.33: Take heed of an evil-doer, for he contriveth wicked things; Lest haply he bring upon you blame forever.
11.34: Receive a stranger into your house, and he will distract you with brawls, And estrange you from your own.

12.1: If you do good, know to whom you do it; And your good deeds will have thanks.
12.2: Do good to a godly man, and you will find a recompense; And if not from him, yet from the Most High.
12.3: There will no good come to him that continueth to do evil, Nor to him that gives no alms.
12.4: Give to the godly man, And help not the sinner.
12.5: Do good to one that is lowly, And give not to an ungodly man: Keep back his bread, and give it not to him, Lest he overmaster you thereby: For you will receive twice as much evil For all the good you will have done to him.
12.6: For the Most High also hates sinners, And will repay vengeance to the ungodly.
12.7: Give to the good man, And help not the sinner.
12.8: A man’s friend will not be fully tried in prosperity; And his enemy will not be hidden in adversity.
12.9: In a man’s prosperity his enemies are grieved; And in his adversity even his friend will be separated from him.
12.10: Never trust your enemy: For like as the brass rusts, so is his wickedness.
12.11: Though he humble himself, and go crouching, Yet take good heed, and beware of him, And you will be to him as one that has wiped a mirror, And you will know that he has not utterly rusted it.
12.12: Set him not by you, Lest he overthrow you and stand in your place; Let him not sit on your right hand, Lest he seek to take your seat, And at the last you acknowledge my words, And be pricked with my sayings.
12.13: Who will pity a charmer that is bitten with a serpent, Or any that come near wild beasts?
12.14: Even so who will pity him that goes to a sinner, And is mingled with him in his sins?
12.15: For a while he will abide with you, And if you give way, he will not hold out.
12.16: And the enemy will speak sweetly with his lips, And in his heart take counsel how to overthrow you into a pit: The enemy will weep with his eyes, And if he find opportunity, he will not be satiated with blood.
12.17: If adversity meet you, you will find him there before you; And as though he would help you, he will trip up your heel.
12.18: He will shake his head, and clap his hands, And whisper much, and change his countenance.

13.1: He that touches pitch will be defiled; And he that has fellowship with a proud man will become like to him.
13.2: Take not up a burden above your strength; And have no fellowship with one that is mightier and richer than yourself. What fellowship shall the earthen pot have with the kettle? This will strike, and that will be dashed in pieces.
13.3: The rich man does a wrong, and he threatens withal: The poor is wronged, and he will entreat withal.
13.4: If you be profitable, he will make merchandise of you; And if you be in lack, he will forsake you.
13.5: If you have substance, he will live with you; And he will make you bare, and will not be sorry.
13.6: Hath he had need of you? then he will deceive you, And smile upon you, and give you hope: He will speak you fair, and say, What need you?
13.7: And he will shame you by his meats, Until he have made you bare twice or thrice, And at the last he will laugh you to scorn: Afterward will he see you, and will forsake you, And shake his head at you.
13.8: Beware that you be not deceived, and brought low in your mirth.
13.9: If a mighty man invite you, be retiring, And so much the more will he invite you.
13.10: Press not upon him, lest you be thrust back; And stand not far off, lest you be forgotten.
13.11: Affect not to speak with him as an equal, And believe not his many words: For with much talk will he try you, And in a smiling manner will search you out.
13.12: He that keeps not to himself words spoken is unmerciful; And he will not spare to hurt and to bind.
13.13: Keep them to yourself, and take earnest heed, For you walk in peril of your falling.
13.15: Every living creature loves his like, And every man loves his neighbor.
13.16: All flesh consorts according to kind, And a man will cleave to his like.
13.17: What fellowship shall the wolf have with the lamb? So is the sinner to the godly.
13.18: What peace is there between the hyena and the dog? And what peace between the rich man and the poor?
13.19: Wild asses are the prey of lions in the wilderness; So poor men are pasture for the rich.
13.20: Lowliness is an abomination to a proud man; So a poor man is an abomination to the rich.
13.21: A rich man when he is shaken is held up of his friends; But one of low degree being down is thrust away also by his friends.
13.22: When a rich man is fallen, there are many helpers; He speaks things not to be spoken, and men justify him: A man of low degree falls, and men rebuke him withal; He utters wisdom, and no place is allowed him.
13.23: A rich man speaks, and all keep silence; And what he says they extol to the clouds: A poor man speaks, and they say, Who is this? And if he stumble, they will help to overthrow him.
13.24: Riches are good that have no sin; And poverty is evil in the mouth of the ungodly.
13.25: The heart of a man changes his countenance, Whether it be for good or for evil.
13.26: A cheerful countenance is a token of a heart that is in prosperity; And the finding out of parables is a weariness of thinking.

14.1: Blessed is the man that has not slipped with his mouth, And is not pricked with sorrow for sins.
14.2: Blessed is he whose soul does not condemn him, And who is not fallen from his hope.
14.3: Riches are not comely for a niggard; And what should an envious man do with money?
14.4: He that gathers by taking from his own soul gathers for others; And others will revel in his goods.
14.5: He that is evil to himself, to whom will he be good? And he will not rejoice in his possessions.
14.6: There is none more evil than he that envies himself; And this is a recompense of his wickedness.
14.7: Even if he does good, he does it in forgetfulness; And at the last he shows forth his wickedness.
14.8: Evil is he that envies with his eye, Turning away the face, and despising the souls of men.
14.9: A covetous man’s eye is not satisfied with his portion; And wicked injustice dries up his soul.
14.10: An evil eye is grudging of bread, And he is miserly at his table
14.11: My son, according as you have, do well to yourself, And bring offerings to the Lord worthily.
14.12: Remember that death will not wait, And that the covenant of the grave is not showed to you.
14.13: Do well to your friend before you die; And according to your ability stretch out your hand and give to him.
14.14: Defraud not yourself of a good day; And don’t let the portion of a good desire pass you by.
14.15: Shall you not leave your labors to another? And your toils to be divided by lot?
14.16: Give, and take, and decieve your soul; For there is no seeking of luxury in the grave.
14.17: All flesh waxes old as a garment; For the covenant from the beginning is, You shall die the death.
14.18: As of the leaves flourishing on a thick tree, Some it sheds, and some it makes to grow; So also of the generations of flesh and blood, One comes to an end, and another is born.
14.19: Every work rots and falls away, And the worker thereof shall depart with it.
14.20: Blessed is the man that shall meditate in wisdom, And that shall discourse by his understanding.
14.21: He that considers her ways in his heart Shall also have knowledge in her secrets.
14.22: Go forth after her as one that tracketh, And lie in wait in her ways.
14.23: He that pries in at her windows Shall also hearken at her doors.
14.24: He that lodges close to her house Shall also fasten a nail in her walls.
14.25: He shall pitch his tent near at hand to her, And will lodge in a lodging where good things are.
14.26: He will set his children under her shelter, And will rest under her branches.
14.27: By her he will be covered from heat, And will lodge in her glory.

15.1: He that fears the Lord will do this; And he that has possession of the law will obtain her.
15.2: And as a mother shall she meet him, And receive him as a wife married in her virginity.
15.3: With bread of understanding will she feed him, And give him water of wisdom to drink.
15.4: He will be stayed upon her, and will not be moved; And will rely upon her, and will not be confounded.
15.5: And she will exalt him above his neighbors; And in the midst of the congregation will she open his mouth.
15.6: He will inherit joy, and a crown of gladness, And an everlasting name.
15.7: Foolish men will not obtain her; And sinners will not see her.
15.8: She is far from pride; And liars will not remember her.
15.9: Praise is not comely in the mouth of a sinner; For it was not sent him from the Lord.
15.10: For praise will be spoken in wisdom; And the Lord will prosper it.
15.11: Say not you, It is through the Lord that I fell away; For you shall not do the things that he hates.
15.12: Say not you, It is he that caused me to err; For he has no need of a sinful man.
15.13: The Lord hates every abomination; And those who fear him love it not.
15.14: He himself made man from the beginning, And left him in the hand of his own counsel.
15.15: If you will, you shall keep the commandments; And to perform faithfulness is of your own good pleasure.
15.16: He has set fire and water before you: You will stretch forth your hand to whichever you will.
15.17: Before man is life and death; And whichever he likes, it shall be given him.
15.18: For great is the wisdom of the Lord: He is mighty in power, and sees all things;
15.19: And his eyes are upon those who fear him; And he will take knowledge of every work of man.
15.20: He has not commanded any man to be ungodly; And he has not given any man licence to sin.

16.1: Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children, Neither delight in ungodly sons.
16.2: If they multiply, delight not in them, Except the fear of the Lord be with them.
16.3: Trust not you in their life, Neither rely on their condition: For one is better than a thousand; And to die childless than to have ungodly children.
16.4: For from one that has understanding will a city be peopled; But a race of wicked men will be made desolate.
16.5: Many such things I have seen with my eyes; And my ear has heard mightier things than these.
16.6: In the congregation of sinners will a fire be kindled; And in a disobedient nation wrath is kindled.
16.7: He was not pacified toward the giants of old time, Who revolted in their strength.
16.8: He spared not those with whom Lot sojourned, Whom he abhorred for their pride.
16.9: He pitied not the people of perdition, Who were taken away in their sins.
16.10: And in like manner the six hundred thousand footmen, Who were gathered together in the hardness of their hearts.
16.11: Even if there be one stiff-necked person, It is marvel if he will be unpunished: For mercy and wrath are with him; He is mighty to forgive, and he pours out wrath.
16.12: As his mercy is great, so is his correction also: He judges a man according to his works.
16.13: The sinner will not escape with his plunder; And the perseverance of the godly will not be frustrated.
16.14: He will make room for every work of mercy; Each man will find according to his works.
16.17: Don’t say, I shall be hidden from the Lord; And who will remember me from on high? I will not be known among so many people; For what is my soul in a boundless creation?
16.18: Behold, the heaven, and the heaven of heavens, The deep, and the earth, will be moved when he shall visit.
16.19: The mountains and the foundations of the earth together Are shaken with trembling, when he looks upon them.
16.20: And no heart will think upon these things: And who shall conceive his ways?
16.21: And there is a tempest which no man will see; Yes, the more part of his works are hid.
16.22: Who will declare the works of his righteousness? Or who will endure them? For his covenant is afar off.
16.23: He that is lacking in understanding thinks upon these things; And an unwise and erring man thinks follies.
16.24: My son, hearken to me, and learn knowledge, And give heed to my words with your heart.
16.25: I will show forth instruction by weight, And declare knowledge exactly.
16.26: In the judgement of the Lord are his works from the beginning; And from the making of them he disposed the parts thereof.
16.27: He garnished his works forever, And the beginnings of them to their generations: They neither hunger, nor are weary, And they cease not from their works.
16.28: No one thrusteth aside his neighbor; And they will never disobey his word.
16.29: After this also the Lord looked upon the earth, And filled it with his blessings.
16.30: All manner of living things covered the face thereof; And into it is their return.

17.1: The Lord created man of the earth, And turned him back to it again.
17.2: He gave them days by number, and a set time, And gave them authority over the things that are thereon.
17.3: He endued them with strength proper to them; And made them according to his own image.
17.4: He put the fear of man upon all flesh, And gave him to have dominion over beasts and fowls.
17.6: Counsel, and tongue, and eyes, Ears, and heart, gave he them to understand withal.
17.7: He filled them with the knowledge of wisdom, And showed them good and evil.
17.8: He set his eye upon their hearts, To show them the majesty of his works.
17.10: And they will praise the name of his holiness, That they may declare the majesty of his works.
17.11: He added to them knowledge, And gave them a law of life for a heritage.
17.12: He made an everlasting covenant with them, And showed them his judgements.
17.13: Their eyes saw the majesty of his glory; And their ear heard the glory of his voice.
17.14: And he said to them, Beware of all unrighteousness; And he gave them commandment, each man concerning his neighbor.
17.15: Their ways are ever before him; They will not be hid from his eyes.
17.17: For every nation he appointed a ruler; And Israel is the Lord’s portion.
17.19: All their works are as the sun before him; And his eyes are continually upon their ways.
17.20: Their iniquities are not hid from him; And all their sins are before the Lord.
17.22: With him the alms of a man is as a signet; And he will keep the bounty of a man as the apple of the eye.
17.23: Afterwards he will rise up and recompense them, And render their recompense upon their head.
17.24: Howbeit to those who repent he granteth a return; And he comforteth those who are losing patience.
17.25: Return to the Lord, and forsake sins: Make your prayer before his face, and lessen the offence.
17.26: Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from iniquity; And greatly hate the abominable thing.
17.27: Who will give praise to the Most High in the grave, Instead of them which live and return thanks?
17.28: Thanksgiving perishes from the dead, as from one that is not: He that is in life and health will praise the Lord.
17.29: How great is the mercy of the Lord, And his forgiveness to those who turn to him!
17.30: For all things can’t be in men, Because the son of man is not immortal.
17.31: What is brighter than the sun? yet this fails: And an evil man will think on flesh and blood.
17.32: He looks upon the power of the height of heaven: And all men are earth and ashes.

18.1: He that lives forever created all things in common.
18.2: The Lord alone will be justified.
18.4: To none has he given power to declare his works: And who will trace out his mighty deeds?
18.5: Who shall number the strength of his majesty? And who shall also tell out his mercies?
18.6: As for the wondrous works of the Lord, it is not possible to take from them nor add to them, Neither is it possible to track them out.
18.7: When a man has finished, then he is but at the beginning; And when he ceaseth, then will he be in perplexity.
18.8: What is man, and whereto serves he? What is his good, and what is his evil?
18.9: The number of man’s days at the most are a hundred years.
18.10: As a drop of water from the sea, and a pebble from the sand; So are a few years in the day of eternity.
18.11: For this cause the Lord was longsuffering over them, And poured out his mercy upon them.
18.12: He saw and perceived their end, that it is evil; Therefore he multiplied his forgiveness.
18.13: The mercy of a man is upon his neighbor; But the mercy of the Lord is upon all flesh; Reproving, and chastening, and teaching, And bringing again, as a shepherd does his flock.
18.14: He has mercy on those who accept chastening, And that diligently seek after his judgements.
18.15: My son, to your good deeds add no blemish; And no grief of words in any of your giving.
18.16: Shall not the dew assuage the scorching heat? So is a word better than a gift.
18.17: Behold, is not a word better than a gift? And both are with a gracious man.
18.18: A fool will upbrade ungraciously; And the gift of an envious man consumes the eyes.
18.19: Learn before you speak; And have a care of your health or ever you be sick.
18.20: Before judgement examine yourself; And in the hour of visitation you will find forgiveness.
18.21: Humble yourself before you be sick; And in the time of sins show repentance.
18.22: Let nothing hinder you to pay your vow in due time; And wait not until death to be justified.
18.23: Before you make a vow, prepare yourself; And be not as a man that tempts the Lord.
18.24: Think upon the wrath that will be in the days of the end, And the time of vengeance, when he turns away his face.
18.25: In the days of fulness remember the time of hunger, And poverty and lack in the days of wealth.
18.26: From morning until evening the time changes; And all things are speedy before the Lord.
18.27: A wise man will fear in everything; And in days of sinning he will beware of offence.
18.28: Every man of understanding knows wisdom; And he will give thanks to him that found her.
18.29: They that were of understanding in sayings became also wise themselves, And poured forth apt proverbs.
18.30: Go not after your lusts; And refrain yourself from your appetites.
18.31: If you give fully to your soul the delight of her desire, She will make you the laughing stock of your enemies.
18.32: Make not merry in much luxury; Neither be tied to the expense thereof.
18.33: Be not made a beggar by banqueting upon borrowing, When you have nothing in your purse.

19.1: A workman that is a drunkard will not become rich: He that despises small things will fall by little and little.
19.2: Wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away: And he that cleaves to harlots will be the more reckless.
19.3: Moths and worms will have him to heritage; And a reckless soul will be taken away.
19.4: He that is hasty to trust is light-minded; And he that sins will offend against his own soul.
19.5: He that makes merry in his heart will be condemned:
19.6: And he that hates talk has the less wickedness.
19.7: Never repeat what is told you, And you will fare never the worse.
19.8: Whether it be of friend or foe, tell it not; And unless it is a sin to you, reveal it not.
19.9: For he has heard you, and observed you, And when the time comes he will hate you.
19.10: Hast you heard a word? let it die with you: Be of good courage, it will not burst you.
19.11: A fool will travail in pain with a word, As a woman in labor with a child.
19.12: As an arrow that sticks in the flesh of the thigh, So is a word in a fool’s belly.
19.13: Reprove a friend; it may be he did it not: And if he did something, that he may do it no more.
19.14: Reprove your neighbor; it may be he said it not: And if he has said it, that he may not say it again.
19.15: Reprove a friend; for many times there is slander: And trust not every word.
19.16: There is one that slips, and not from the heart: And who is he that has not sinned with his tongue?
19.17: Reprove your neighbor before you threaten him; And give place to the law of the Most High.
19.20: All wisdom is the fear of the Lord; And in all wisdom is the doing of the law.
19.22: And the knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom; And the prudence of sinners is not counsel.
19.23: There is a wickedness, and the same is abomination; And there is a fool lacking in wisdom.
19.24: Better is one that has small understanding, and fears, Than one that has much prudence, and transgresses the law.
19.25: There is an exquisite subtlety, and the same is unjust; And there is one that perverteth favor to gain a judgement.
19.26: There is one that does wickedly, that hangs down his head with mourning; But inwardly he is full of deceit,
19.27: Bowing down his face, and making as if he were deaf of one ear: Where he is not known, he will be beforehand with you.
19.28: And if for lack of power he be hindered from sinning, If he find opportunity, he will do mischief.
19.29: A man will be known by his look, And one that has understanding will be known by his face, when you meet him.
19.30: A man’s attire, and grinning laughter, And gait, show what he is.

20.1: There is a reproof that is not comely; And there is a man that keeps silence, and he is wise.
20.2: How good is it to reprove, rather than to be angry; And he that makes confession will be kept back from hurt.
20.4: As is the lust of an eunuch to deflower a virgin; So is he that executes judgements with violence.
20.5: There is one that keeps silence, and is found wise; And there is one that is hated for his much talk.
20.6: There is one that keeps silence, for he has no answer to make; And there is that keeps silence, as knowing his time.
20.7: A wise man will be silent till his time come; But the braggart and fool will overpass his time.
20.8: He that uses many words will be abhorred; And he that takes to himself authority therein will be hated.
20.9: There is a prosperity that a man finds in misfortunes; And there is a gain that turns to loss.
20.10: There is a gift that will not profit you; And there is a gift whose recompense is double.
20.11: There is an abasement because of glory; And there is that has lifted up his head from a low estate.
20.12: There is that buys much for a little, And pays for it again sevenfold.
20.13: He that is wise in words will make himself beloved; But the pleasantries of fools will be wasted.
20.14: The gift of a fool will not profit you; For his eyes are many instead of one.
20.15: He will give little, and upbraid much; And he will open his mouth like a crier: Today he will lend, and tomorrow he will ask it again: Such an one is a hateful man.
20.16: The fool will say, I have no friend, And I have no thanks for my good deeds; They that eat my bread are of evil tongue.
20.17: How often, and of how many, will he be laughed to scorn!
20.18: A slip on a pavement is better than a slip with the tongue; So the fall of the wicked will come speedily.
20.19: A man without grace is as a tale out of season: It will be continually in the mouth of the ignorant.
20.20: A wise sentence from a fool’s mouth will be rejected; For he will not speak it in its season.
20.21: There is that is hindered from sinning through lack; And when he takes rest, he will not be troubled.
20.22: There is that destroys his soul through bashfulness; And by a foolish countenance he will destroy it.
20.23: There is that for bashfulness promises to his friend; And he makes him his enemy for nothing.
20.24: A lie is a foul blot in a man: It will be continually in the mouth of the ignorant.
20.25: A thief is better than a man that is continually lying: But they both will inherit destruction.
20.26: The disposition of a liar is dishonor; And his shame is with him continually.
20.27: He that is wise in words will advance himself; And one that is prudent will please great men.
20.28: He that tils his land will raise his heap high; And he that pleases great men will get pardon for iniquity.
20.29: Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, And as a muzzle on the mouth, turn away reproofs.
20.30: Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is out of sight, What profit is in them both?
20.31: Better is a man that hides his folly Than a man that hides his wisdom.

21.1: My son, have you sinned? add no more thereto; And make supplication for your former sins.
21.2: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent; For if you draw near it will bite you: The teeth thereof are the teeth of a lion, Slaying the souls of men.
21.3: All iniquity is as a two-edged sword; Its stroke has no healing.
21.4: Terror and violence will lay waste riches; So the house of a haughty man will be laid waste.
21.5: Supplication from a poor man’s mouth reaches to the ears of God, And his judgement comes speedily.
21.6: One that hates reproof is in the path of the sinner; And he that fears the Lord will turn again in his heart.
21.7: He that is mighty in tongue is known afar off: But the man of understanding knows when he slips.
21.8: He that builds his house with other men’s money Is like one that gathers himself stones against winter.
21.9: The congregation of wicked men is as tow wrapped together; And the end of them is a flame of fire.
21.10: The way of sinners is made smooth with stones; And at the last end thereof is the pit of Hades.
21.11: He that keeps the law becomes master of the intent thereof; And the end of the fear of the Lord is wisdom.
21.12: He that is not clever will not be instructed; And there is a cleverness which makes bitterness to abound.
21.13: The knowledge of a wise man will be made to abound as a flood; And his counsel as a fountain of life.
21.14: The inward parts of a fool are like a broken vessel; And he will hold no knowledge.
21.15: If a man of knowledge hear a wise word, He will commend it, and add to it: The dissolute man hears it, and it displeases him, And he puts it away behind his back.
21.16: The discourse of a fool is like a burden in the way; But grace will be found on the lips of the wise.
21.17: The mouth of the prudent man will be sought for in the congregation; And they will ponder his words in their heart.
21.18: As a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool; And the knowledge of an unwise man is as talk without sense.
21.19: Instruction is as fetters on the feet of an unwise man, And as manacles on the right hand.
21.20: A fool lifts up his voice with laughter; But a clever man will scarce smile quietly.
21.21: Instruction is to a prudent man as an ornament of gold, And as a bracelet upon his right arm.
21.22: The foot of a fool is soon in another man’s house; But a man of experience will be ashamed of entering.
21.23: A foolish man peepeth in from the door of another man’s house; But a man that is instructed will stand without.
21.24: It is a lack of instruction in a man to listen at the door; But the prudent man will be grieved with the disgrace.
21.25: The lips of strangers will be grieved at these things; But the words of prudent men will be weighed in the balance.
21.26: The heart of fools is in their mouth; But the mouth of wise men is their heart.
21.27: When the ungodly curses Satan, He curses his own soul.
21.28: A whisperer defiles his own soul, And will be hated wherever he sojourneth.

22.1: A slothful man is compared to a stone that is defiled; And every one will hiss him out in his disgrace.
22.2: A slothful man is compared to the filth of a dunghill: Every man that takes it up will shake out his hand.
22.3: A father has shame in having begotten an uninstructed son; And a foolish daughter is born to his loss.
22.4: A prudent daughter will inherit a husband of her own; And she that brings shame is the grief of her father.
22.5: She that is bold brings shame upon father and husband; And she will be despised of them both.
22.6: Unseasonable discourse is as music in mourning; But stripes and correction are wisdom at every season.
22.7: He that teaches a fool is as one that glues a potsherd together; Even as one that wakes a sleeper out of a deep sleep.
22.8: He that discourseth to a fool is as one discoursing to a man that slumbereth; And at the end he will say, What is it?
22.11: Weep for the dead, for light has failed him; And weep for a fool, for understanding has failed him: Weep more sweetly for the dead, because he has found rest; But the life of the fool is worse than death.
22.12: Seven days are the days of mourning for the dead; But for a fool and an ungodly man, all the days of his life.
22.13: Talk not much with a foolish man, And go not to one that has no understanding: Beware of him, lest you have trouble; And so you shall not be defiled in his onslaught: Turn away from him, and you will find rest; And so you shall not be wearied in his madness.
22.14: What shall be heavier than lead? And what is the name thereof, but a fool?
22.15: Sand, and salt, and a mass of iron, is easier to bear, Than a man without understanding.
22.16: Timber girded and bound into a building will not be loosed with shaking: So a heart established in due season on well advised counsel will not be afraid.
22.17: A heart settled upon a thoughtful understanding Is as an ornament of plaister on a polished wall.
22.18: Pales set on a high place will not stand against the wind: So a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool will not stand against any fear.
22.19: He that pricks the eye will make tears to fall; And he that pricks the heart makes it to show feeling.
22.20: Whoso casts a stone at birds frays them away; And he that upbraids a friend will dissolve friendship.
22.21: If you have drawn a sword against a friend, despair not; For there may be a returning.
22.22: If you have opened your mouth against a friend, fear not; For there may be a reconciling; Except it be for upbraiding, and arrogance, and disclosing of a secret, and a treacherous blow: For these things every friend will flee.
22.23: Gain trust with your neighbor in his poverty, That in his prosperity you may have gladness: Abide stedfast to him in the time of his affliction, That you may be heir with him in his inheritance.
22.24: Before fire is the vapor and smoke of a furnace; So revilings before bloodshed.
22.25: I will not be ashamed to shelter a friend; And I will not hide myself from his face:
22.26: And if any evil happen to me because of him, Every one that hears it will beware of him.
22.27: Who shall set a watch over my mouth, And a seal of shrewdness upon my lips, That I fall not from it, and that my tongue destroy me not?

23.1: O Lord, Father and Master of my life, Abandon me not to their counsel: Suffer me not to fall by them.
23.2: Who will set scourges over my thought, And a discipline of wisdom over my heart? That they spare me not for my ignorances, And my heart pass not by their sins:
23.3: That my ignorances be not multiplied, And my sins abound not; And I will fall before my adversaries, And my enemy rejoice over me.
23.4: O Lord, Father and God of my life, Give me not a proud look,
23.5: And turn away concupiscense from me.
23.6: Let not greediness and chambering overtake me; And give me not over to a shameless mind.
23.7: Hear you, my children, the discipline of the mouth; And he that keeps it will not be taken.
23.8: The sinner will be overtaken in his lips; And the reviler and the proud man will stumble therein.
23.9: Accustom not your mouth to an oath; And be not accustomed to the naming of the Holy One.
23.10: For as a servant that is continually scourged will not lack a bruise, So he also that swears and names God continually will not be cleansed from sin.
23.11: A man of many oaths will be filled with iniquity; And the scourge will not depart from his house: If he shall offend, his sin will be upon him; And if he disregard it, he has sinned doubly; And if he has sworn in vain, he will not be justified; For his house will be filled with calamities.
23.12: There is a manner of speech that is clothed about with death: Let it not be found in the heritage of Jacob; For all these things will be far from the godly, And they will not wallow in sins.
23.13: Accustom not your mouth to gross rudeness, For therein is the word of sin.
23.14: Remember your father and your mother, For you sit in the midst of great men; That you be not forgetful before them, And become a fool by your custom; So will you wish that you had not been born, And curse the day of your nativity.
23.15: A man that is accustomed to words of reproach Will not be corrected all the days of his life.
23.16: Two sorts of men multiply sins, And the third will bring wrath: A hot mind, as a burning fire, will not be quenched till it be consumed: A fornicator in the body of his flesh will never cease till he has burned out the fire.
23.17: All bread is sweet to a fornicator: He will not leave off till he die.
23.18: A man that goes astray from his own bed, Saying in his heart, Who sees me? Darkness is round about me, and the walls hide me, And no man sees me; of whom am I afraid? The Most High will not remember my sins;
23.19: —And the eyes of men are his terror, And he knows not that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, Beholding all the ways of men, And looking into secret places.
23.20: All things were known to him or ever they were created; And in like manner also after they were perfected.
23.21: This man will be punished in the streets of the city; And where he suspected not he will be taken.
23.22: So also a wife that leaves her husband, And brings in an heir by a stranger.
23.23: For first, she was disobedient in the law of the Most High; And secondly, she trespassed against her own husband; And thirdly, she played the adulteress in whoredom, And brought in children by a stranger.
23.24: She shall be brought out into the congregation; And upon her children will there be visitation.
23.25: Her children will not spread into roots, And her branches will bear no fruit.
23.26: She will leave her memory for a curse; And her reproach will not be blotted out.
23.27: And those who are left behind will know that there is nothing better than the fear of the Lord, And nothing sweeter than to take heed to the commandments of the Lord.

24.1: Wisdom will praise herself, And will glory in the midst of her people.
24.2: In the congregation of the Most High will she open her mouth, And glory in the presence of his power.
24.3: I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, And covered the earth as a mist.
24.4: I lived in high places, And my throne is in the pillar of the cloud.
24.5: Alone I compassed the circuit of heaven, And walked in the depth of the abyss.
24.6: In the waves of the sea, and in all the earth, And in every people and nation, I got a possession.
24.7: With all these I sought rest; And in whose inheritance shall I lodge?
24.8: Then the Creator of all things gave me a commandment; And he that created me made my tabernacle to rest, And said, Let your tabernacle be in Jacob, And your inheritance in Israel.
24.9: He created me from the beginning before the world; And to the end I will not fail.
24.10: In the holy tabernacle I ministered before him; And so was I established in Sion.
24.11: In the beloved city likewise he gave me rest; And in Jerusalem was my authority.
24.12: And I took root in a people that was glorified, Even in the portion of the Lord’s own inheritance.
24.13: I was exalted like a cedar in Libanus, And as a cypress tree on the mountains of Hermon.
24.14: I was exalted like a palm tree on the sea shore, And as rose plants in Jericho, And as a fair olive tree in the plain; And I was exalted as a plane tree.
24.15: As cinnamon and aspalathus, I have given a scent of perfumes; And as choice myrrh, I spread abroad a pleasant odour; As galbanum, and onyx, and stacte, And as the fume of frankincense in the tabernacle.
24.16: As the terebinth I stretched out my branches; And my branches are branches of glory and grace.
24.17: As the vine I put forth grace; And my flowers are the fruit of glory and riches.
24.19: Come to me, you that are desirous of me, And be you filled with my produce.
24.20: For my memorial is sweeter than honey, And my inheritance than the honeycomb.
24.21: They that eat me will yet be hungry; And those who drink me will yet be thirsty.
24.22: He that obeys me will not be ashamed; And those who work in me will not do amiss.
24.23: All these things are the book of the covenant of the Most High God, Even the law which Moses commanded us for a heritage to the assemblies of Jacob.
24.25: It is he that makes wisdom abundant, as Pishon, And as Tigris in the days of new fruits;
24.26: That makes understanding full as Euphrates, And as Jordan in the days of harvest;
24.27: That makes instruction to shine forth as the light, As Gihon in the days of vintage.
24.28: The first man knew her not perfectly; And in like manner the last has not traced her out.
24.29: For her thoughts are filled from the sea, And her counsels from the great deep.
24.30: And I came out as a stream from a river, And as a conduit into a garden.
24.31: I said, I will water my garden, And will water abundantly my garden bed; And, behold, my stream became a river, And my river became a sea.
24.32: I will yet bring instruction to light as the morning, And will make these things to shine forth afar off.
24.33: I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, And leave it to generations of ages.
24.34: Behold that I have not laboured for myself only, But for all those who diligently seek her.

25.1: In three things I was beautified, And stood up beautiful before the Lord and men: The concord of kindred, and friendship of neighbors, And a woman and her husband that walk together in agreement.
25.2: But three sorts of men my soul hates, And I am greatly offended at their life: A poor man that is haughty, and a rich man that is a liar, And an old man that is an adulterer lacking understanding.
25.3: In your youth you have not gathered, And how should you find in your old age?
25.4: How beautiful a thing is judgement for gray hairs, And for elders to know counsel!
25.5: How beautiful is the wisdom of old men, And thought and counsel to men that are in honor!
25.6: Much experience is the crown of old men; And their glorying is the fear of the Lord.
25.7: There be nine things that I have thought of, and in my heart counted happy; And the tenth I will utter with my tongue: A man that has joy of his children; A man that lives and looks upon the fall of his enemies:
25.8: Happy is he that dwells with a wife of understanding; And he that has not slipped with his tongue; And he that has not served a man that is unworthy of him:
25.9: Happy is he that has found prudence; And he that discourseth in the ears of those who listen.
25.10: How great is he that has found wisdom! Yet is there none above him that fears the Lord.
25.11: The fear of the Lord passes all things: He that holds it, to whom shall he be likened?
25.13: Give me any plague but the plague of the heart; And any wickedness but the wickedness of a woman;
25.14: Any calamity, but a calamity from those who hate me; And any vengeance, but the vengeance of enemies.
25.15: There is no head above the head of a serpent; And there is no wrath above the wrath of an enemy.
25.16: I will rather dwell with a lion and a dragon, Than keep house with a wicked woman.
25.17: The wickedness of a woman changes her look, And darkens her countenance as a bear does.
25.18: Her husband will sit at meat among his neighbors, And when he hears it he sighs bitterly.
25.19: All malice is but little to the malice of a woman: Let the portion of a sinner fall on her.
25.20: As the going up a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, So is a wife full of words to a quiet man.
25.21: Throw not yourself upon the beauty of a woman; And desire not a woman for her beauty.
25.22: There is anger, and impudence, and great reproach, If a woman maintain her husband.
25.23: A wicked woman is abasement of heart, And sadness of countenance, and a wounded heart: A woman that will not make her husband happy Is as hands that hang down, and palsied knees.
25.24: From a woman was the beginning of sin; And because of her we all die.
25.25: Give not water an outlet; Neither to a wicked woman freedom of speech.
25.26: If she go not as you would have her, Cut her off from your flesh.

26.1: Happy is the husband of a good wife; And the number of his days will be twofold.
26.2: A brave woman rejoices her husband; And he will fulfil his years in peace.
26.3: A good wife is a good portion: She will be given in the portion of such as fear the Lord.
26.4: Whether a man be rich or poor, A good heart makes at all times a cheerful countenance.
26.5: Of three things my heart was afraid; And concerning the fourth kind I made supplication: The slander of a city, and the assembly of a multitude, and a false accusation: All these are more grievous than death.
26.6: A grief of heart and sorrow is a woman that is jealous of another woman, And the scourge of a tongue communicating to all.
26.7: A wicked woman is as a yoke of oxen shaken to and fro: He that takes hold of her is as one that graspeth a scorpion.
26.8: A drunken woman causes great wrath; And she will not cover her own shame.
26.9: The whoredom of a woman is in the lifting up of her eyes; And it will be known by her eyelids.
26.10: Keep strict watch on a headstrong daughter, Lest she find liberty for herself, and use it.
26.11: Look well after an impudent eye; And marvel not if it trespass against you.
26.12: She will open her mouth, as a thirsty traveller, And drink of every water that is near: At every post will she sit down, And open her quiver against any arrow.
26.13: The grace of a wife will delight her husband; And her knowledge will fatten his bones.
26.14: A silent woman is a gift of the Lord; And there is nothing so much worth as a well-instructed soul.
26.15: A shamefast woman is grace upon grace; And there is no price worthy of a continent soul.
26.16: As the sun when it arises in the highest places of the Lord, So is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of a man’s house.
26.17: As the lamp that shineth upon the holy candlestick, So is the beauty of the face in ripe age.
26.18: As the golden pillars are upon a base of silver, So are beautiful feet with the breasts of one that is stedfast.
26.28: For two things my heart is grieved; And for the third anger comes upon me: A man of war that suffers for poverty; And men of understanding that are counted as refuse: One that turns back from righteousness to sin; The Lord will prepare him for the sword.
26.29: A merchant shall hardly keep himself from wrong doing; And a huckster will not be acquitted of sin.

27.1: Many have sinned for a thing indifferent; And he that seeks to multiply gain will turn his eye away.
27.2: A nail will stick fast between the joinings of stones; And sin will thrust itself in between buying and selling.
27.3: Unless a man hold on diligently in the fear of the Lord, His house will soon be overthrown.
27.4: In the shaking of a sieve, the refuse remains; So the filth of man in his reasoning.
27.5: The furnace will prove the potter’s vessels; And the trial of a man is in his reasoning.
27.6: The fruit of a tree declares the husbandry thereof; So is the utterance of the thought of the heart of a man.
27.7: Praise no man before you hear him reason; For this is the trial of men.
27.8: If you follow righteousness, you will obtain her, And put her on, as a long robe of glory.
27.9: Birds will resort to their like; And truth will return to those who practise her.
27.10: The lion lies in wait for prey; So does sin for those who work iniquity.
27.11: The discourse of a godly man is always wisdom: But the foolish man changes as the moon.
27.12: Among men void of understanding observe the opportunity; But stay continually among the thoughtful.
27.13: The discourse of fools is an offence; And their laughter is in the wantonness of sin.
27.14: The talk of a man of many oaths will make the hair stand upright; And their strife makes one stop his ears.
27.15: The strife of the proud is a shedding of blood; And their reviling of each other is a grievous thing to hear.
27.16: He that reveals secrets destroys credit, And will not find a friend to his mind.
27.17: Love a friend, and keep faith with him: But if you reveal his secrets, You shall not pursue after him;
27.18: For as a man has destroyed his enemy, So have you destroyed the friendship of your neighbor.
27.19: And as a bird which you have loosed out of your hand, So have you let your neighbor go, and you will not catch him again:
27.20: Pursue him not, for he is gone far away, And has escaped as a gazelle out of the snare.
27.21: For a wound may be bound up, and after reviling there may be a reconcilement; But he that reveals secrets has lost hope.
27.22: One that winks with the eye contriveth evil things; And no man will remove him from it.
27.23: When you are present, he will speak sweetly, And will admire your words; But afterward he will writhe his mouth, And set a trap for you in your words.
27.24: I have hated many things, but nothing like him; And the Lord will hate him.
27.25: One that casts a stone on high casts it on his own head; And a deceitful stroke will open wounds.
27.26: He that digs a pit will fall into it; And he that sets a snare will be taken therein.
27.27: He that does evil things, they will roll upon him, And he will not know whence they have come to him.
27.28: Mockery and reproach are from the haughty; And vengeance, as a lion, will lie in wait for him.
27.29: They that rejoice at the fall of the godly will be taken in a snare; And anguish will consume them before they die.
27.30: Wrath and anger, these also are abominations; And a sinful man will possess them.

28.1: He that takes vengeance will find vengeance from the Lord; And he will surely make firm his sins.
28.2: Forgive your neighbor the hurt that he has done you; And then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.
28.3: Man cherisheth anger against man; And does he seek healing from the Lord?
28.4: Upon a man like himself he has no mercy; And does he make supplication for his own sins?
28.5: He being himself flesh nourishes wrath: Who will make atonement for his sins?
28.6: Remember your last end, and cease from enmity: Remember corruption and death, and abide in the commandments.
28.7: Remember the commandments, and be not angry with your neighbor; And remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.
28.8: Abstain from strife, and you will diminish your sins: For a passionate man will kindle strife;
28.9: And a man that is a sinner will trouble friends, And will make debate among those who are at peace.
28.10: As is the fuel of the fire, so will it burn; And as the stoutness of the strife is, so will it burn: As is the strength of the man, so will be his wrath; And as is his wealth, so will he exalt his anger.
28.11: A contention begun in haste kindles a fire; And a hasty fighting sheds blood.
28.12: If you blow a spark, it will burn; And if you spit upon it, it will be quenched: And both these shall come out of your mouth.
28.13: Curse the whisperer and double-tongued: For he has destroyed many that were at peace.
28.14: A third person’s tongue has shaken many, And dispersed them from nation to nation; And it has pulled down strong cities, And overthrown the houses of great men.
28.15: A third person’s tongue has cast out brave women, And deprived them of their labors.
28.16: He that hearkens to it will not find rest, Nor shall he dwell quietly.
28.17: The stroke of a whip makes a mark in the flesh; But the stroke of a tongue will break bones.
28.18: Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: Yet not so many as those who have fallen because of the tongue.
28.19: Happy is he that is sheltered from it, That has not passed through the wrath thereof; That has not drawn its yoke, And has not been bound with its bands.
28.20: For the yoke thereof is a yoke of iron, And the bands thereof are bands of brass.
28.21: The death thereof is an evil death; And Hades were better than it.
28.22: It shall not have rule over godly men; And they shall not be burned in its flame.
28.23: They that forsake the Lord shall fall into it; And it shall burn among them, and shall not be quenched: It shall be sent forth upon them as a lion; And as a leopard it shall destroy them.
28.24: Look that you hedge your possession about with thorns; Bind up your silver and your gold;
28.25: And make a balance and a weight for your words; And make a door and a bar for your mouth.
28.26: Take heed lest you slip therein; Lest you fall before one that lies in wait.

29.1: He that shows mercy will lend to his neighbor; And he that strengthens him with his hand keeps the commandments.
29.2: Lend to your neighbor in time of his need; And pay you your neighbor again in due season.
29.3: Confirm your word, and keep faith with him; And at all seasons you shall find what you need.
29.4: Many have reckoned a loan as a windfall, And have given trouble to those that helped them.
29.5: Till he has received, he will kiss a man’s hands; And for his neighbor’s money he will speak submissly: And when payment is due, he will prolong the time, And return words of heaviness, and complain of the times.
29.6: If he prevail, he shall hardly receive the half; And he will count it as a windfall: If not, he has deprived him of his money, And he has gotten him for an enemy without cause: He will pay him with cursings and railings; And for honor he will pay him disgrace.
29.7: Many on account of men’s ill-dealing have turned away; They have feared to be defrauded for nothing.
29.8: Howbeit with a man in poor estate be longsuffering; And let him not wait for your alms.
29.9: Help a poor man for the commandment’s sake; And according to his need send him not empty away.
29.10: Lose your money for a brother and a friend; And let it not rust under the stone to be lost.
29.11: Bestow your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High; And it shall profit you more than gold.
29.12: Shut up alms in your store-chambers; And it shall deliver you out of all affliction:
29.13: It shall fight for you against your enemy Better than a mighty shield and a ponderous spear.
29.14: A good man will be surety for his neighbor; And he that has lost shame will fail him.
29.15: Forget not the good offices of your surety; For he has given his life for you.
29.16: A sinner will overthrow the good estate of his surety;
29.17: And he that is of an unthankful mind will fail him that delivered him.
29.18: Suretiship has undone many that were prospering, And shaken them as a wave of the sea: Mighty men has it driven from their homes; And they wandered among strange nations.
29.19: A sinner that falls into suretiship, And undertakes contracts for work, shall fall into lawsuits.
29.20: Help your neighbor according to your power, And take heed to yourself that you fall not to the same.
29.21: The chief thing for life is water, and bread, And a garment, and a house to cover shame.
