29.22: Better is the life of a poor man under a shelter of logs, Than sumptuous fare in another man’s house.
29.23: With little or with much, be well satisfied.
29.24: It is a miserable life to go from house to house: And where you are a sojourner, you shall not dare to open your mouth.
29.25: You shall entertain, and give to drink, and have no thanks: And besides this you shall hear bitter words.
29.26: Come hither, you sojourner, furnish a table, And if you have anything in your hand, feed me with it.
29.27: Go forth, you sojourner, from the face of honor; My brother is come to be my guest; I have need of my house.
29.28: These things are grievous to a man of understanding; The upbraiding of house-room, and the reproaching of the money-lender.

30.1: He that loves his son will continue to lay stripes upon him, That he may have joy of him in the end.
30.2: He that chastises his son shall have profit of him, And shall glory of him among his acquaintance.
30.3: He that teaches his son shall provoke his enemy to jealousy; And before friends he shall rejoice of him.
30.4: His father dieth, and is as though he had not died; For he has left one behind him like himself.
30.5: In his life, he saw and rejoiced in him; And when he died, he sorrowed not:
30.6: He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, And one to requite kindness to his friends.
30.7: He that makes too much of his son shall bind up his wounds; And his heart will be troubled at every cry.
30.8: An unbroken horse becomes stubborn; And a son left at large becomes headstrong.
30.9: Cocker your child, and he shall make you afraid: Play with him, and he will grieve you.
30.10: Laugh not with him, lest you have sorrow with him; And you shall gnash your teeth in the end.
30.11: Give him no liberty in his youth, And wink not at his follies.
30.12: Bow down his neck in his youth, And beat him on the sides while he is a child, Lest he wax stubborn, and be disobedient to you; And there shall be sorrow to your soul.
30.13: Chastise your son, and take pains with him, Lest his shameless behavior be an offence to you.
30.14: Better is a poor man, being sound and strong of constitution, Than a rich man that is plagued in his body.
30.15: Health and a good constitution are better than all gold; And a strong body than wealth without measure.
30.16: There is no riches better than health of body; And there is no gladness above the joy of the heart.
30.17: Death is better than a bitter life, And eternal rest than a continual sickness.
30.18: Good things poured out upon a mouth that is closed Are as messes of meat laid upon a grave.
30.19: What does an offering profit an idol? For neither shall it eat nor smell: So is he that is afflicted of the Lord,
30.20: Seeing with his eyes and groaning, As an eunuch embracing a virgin and groaning.
30.21: Give not over your soul to sorrow; And afflict not yourself in your own counsel.
30.22: Gladness of heart is the life of a man; And the joyfulness of a man is length of days.
30.23: Love your own soul, and comfort your heart: And remove sorrow far from you; For sorrow has destroyed many, And there is no profit therein.
30.24: Envy and wrath shorten a man’s days; And care brings old age before the time.
30.25: A cheerful and good heart Will have a care of his meat and diet.

31.1: Wakefulness that comes of riches consumes the flesh, And the anxiety thereof puts away sleep.
31.2: Wakeful anxiety will crave slumber; And in a sore disease sleep will be broken.
31.3: A rich man toileth in gathering money together; And when he rests, he is filled with his good things.
31.4: A poor man toileth in lack of substance; And when he rests, he becomes needy.
31.5: He that loves gold shall not be justified; And he that follows destruction shall himself have his fill of it.
31.6: Many have been given over to ruin for the sake of gold; And their perdition meets them face to face.
31.7: It is a stumbling block to those who sacrifice to it; And every fool shall be taken therewith.
31.8: Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, And that goes not after gold.
31.9: Who is he? and we will call him blessed: For wonderful things has he done among his people.
31.10: Who has been tried thereby, and found perfect? Then let him glory. Who has had the power to transgress, and has not transgressed? And to do evil, and has not done it?
31.11: His goods shall be made sure, And the congregation shall declare his alms.
31.12: Sittest you at a great table? be not greedy upon it, And say not, Many are the things upon it.
31.13: Remember that an evil eye is a wicked thing: What has been created more evil than an eye? Therefore it sheds tears from every face.
31.14: Stretch not your hand wherever it looks, And thrust not yourself with it into the dish.
31.15: Consider your neighbor’s liking by your own; And be discreet in every point.
31.16: Eat, as becomes a man, those things which are set before you; And eat not greedily, lest you be hated.
31.17: Be first to leave off for manners’ sake; And be not insatiable, lest you offend.
31.18: And if you sit among many, Reach not out your hand before them.
31.19: How sufficient to a well-mannered man is a very little, And he does not breathe hard upon his bed.
31.20: Healthy sleep comes of moderate eating; He rises early, and his wits are with him: The pain of wakefulness, and colic, And griping, are with an insatiable man.
31.21: And if you have been forced to eat, Rise up in the midst thereof, and you shall have rest.
31.22: Hear me, my son, and despise me not, And at the last you shall find my words true: In all your works be quick, And no disease shall come to you.
31.23: Him that is liberal of his meat the lips shall bless; And the testimony of his excellence shall be believed.
31.24: Him that is a niggard of his meat the city shall murmur at; And the testimony of his niggardness shall be sure.
31.25: Show not yourself valiant in wine; For wine has destroyed many.
31.26: The furnace proves the temper of steel by dipping; So does wine prove hearts in the quarreling of the proud.
31.27: Wine is as good as life to men, If you drink it in its measure: What life is there to a man that is without wine? And it has been created to make men glad.
31.28: Wine drunk in season and to satisfy Is joy of heart, and gladness of soul:
31.29: Wine drunk largely is bitterness of soul, With provocation and conflict.
31.30: Drunkenness increases the rage of a fool to his hurt; It diminishes strength, and adds wounds.
31.31: Rebuke not your neighbor at a banquet of wine, Neither set him at nothing in his mirth: Speak not to him a word of reproach, And press not upon him by asking back a debt.

32.1: Have they made you ruler of a feast? Be not lifted up, Be you among them as one of them; Take thought for them, and so sit down.
32.2: And when you have done all your office, take your place, That you may be gladdened on their account, And receive a crown for your well ordering.
32.3: Speak, you that are the elder, for it becomes you, but with sound knowledge; And hinder not music.
32.4: Pour not out talk where there is a performance of music, And display not your wisdom out of season.
32.5: As a signet of carbuncle in a setting of gold, So is a concert of music in a banquet of wine.
32.6: As a signet of emerald in a work of gold, So is a strain of music with pleasant wine.
32.7: Speak, young man, if there be need of you; Yet scarcely if you be twice asked.
32.8: Sum up your speech, many things in few words; Be as one that knows and yet holds his tongue.
32.9: If you be among great men, behave not as their equal; And when another is speaking, make not much babbling.
32.10: Before thunder speedeth lightning; And before a shamefast man favor shall go forth.
32.11: Rise up betimes, and be not the last; Get you home quickly and loiter not:
32.12: There take your pastime, and do what is in your heart; And sin not by proud speech:
32.13: And for these things bless him that made you, And gives you to drink freely of his good things.
32.14: He that fears the Lord will receive his discipline; And those who seek him early shall find favor.
32.15: He that seeks the law shall be filled therewith: But the hypocrite shall stumble thereat.
32.16: They that fear the Lord shall find judgement, And shall kindle righteous acts as a light.
32.17: A sinful man shunneth reproof, And will find a judgement according to his will.
32.18: A man of counsel will not neglect a thought; A strange and proud man will not crouch in fear, Even after he has done a thing by himself without counsel.
32.19: Do nothing without counsel; And when you have once done, repent not.
32.20: Go not in a way of conflict; And stumble not in stony places.
32.21: Be not confident in a smooth way.
32.22: And beware of your own children.
32.23: In every work trust your own soul; For this is the keeping of the commandments.
32.24: He that believes the law gives heed to the commandment; And he that trusts in the Lord shall suffer no loss.

33.1: There shall no evil happen to him that fears the Lord; But in temptation once and again will he deliver him.
33.2: A wise man will not hate the law; But he that is a hypocrite therein is as a ship in a storm.
33.3: A man of understanding will put his trust in the law; And the law is faithful to him, as when one asks at the oracle.
33.4: Prepare your speech, and so shall you be heard; Bind up instruction, and make your answer.
33.5: The heart of a fool is as a cartwheel; And his thoughts like a rolling axle tree.
33.6: A stallion horse is as a mocking friend; He neighs under every one that sits upon him.
33.7: Why does one day excel another, When all the light of every day in the year is of the sun?
33.8: By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished; And he varied seasons and feasts:
33.9: Some of them he exalted and hallowed, And some of them has he made ordinary days.
33.10: And all men are from the ground, And Adam was created of earth.
33.11: In the abundance of his knowledge the Lord distinguished them, And made their ways various:
33.12: Some of them he blessed and exalted, And some of them he hallowed and brought near to himself: Some of them he cursed and brought low, And overthrew them from their place.
33.13: As the clay of the potter in his hand, All his ways are according to his good pleasure; So men are in the hand of him that made them, To render to them according to his judgement.
33.14: Good is the opposite of evil, And life is the opposite of death: So is the sinner is the opposite of the godly.
33.15: And thus look upon all the works of the Most High; Two and two, one against another.
33.16: And I waked up last, As one that gleans after the grape gatherers: By the blessing of the Lord I got before them, And filled my winepress as one that gathers grapes.
33.17: Consider that I laboured not for myself alone, But for all those who seek instruction.
33.18: Hear me, you great men of the people, And hearken with your ears, you rulers of the congregation.
33.19: To son and wife, to brother and friend, Give not power over you while you live; And give not your goods to another, Lest you repent and make supplication for them again.
33.20: Whilst you yet live, and breath is in you, Give not yourself over to anybody.
33.21: For better it is that your children should supplicate you, Than that you should look to the hand of your sons.
33.22: In all your works keep the upper hand; Bring not a stain on your honor.
33.23: In the day that you endest the days of your life, And in the time of death, distribute your inheritance.
33.24: Fodder, a stick, and burdens, for an ass; Bread, and discipline, and work, for a servant.
33.25: Set your servant to work, and you shall find rest: Leave his hands idle, and he will seek liberty.
33.26: Yoke and thong will bow the neck: And for an evil servant there are racks and tortures.
33.27: Send him to labor, that he be not idle; For idleness teaches much mischief.
33.28: Set him to work, as is fit for him; And if he obey not, make his fetters heavy.
33.29: And be not excessive toward any; And without judgement do nothing.
33.30: If you have a servant, let him be as yourself, Because you have bought him with blood.
33.31: If you have a servant, treat him as yourself; For as your own soul will you have need of him: If you treat him ill, and he depart and run away, Which way will you go to seek him?

34.1: Vain and false hopes are for a man void of understanding; And dreams give wings to fools.
34.2: As one that catches at a shadow, and follows after the wind, So is he that sets his mind on dreams.
34.3: The vision of dreams is as this thing against that, The likeness of a face near a face.
34.4: Of an unclean thing what shall be cleansed? And of that which is false what shall be true?
34.5: Divinations, and soothsayings, and dreams, are vain: And the heart fancies, as a woman’s in travail.
34.6: If they be not sent from the Most High in your visitation, Give not your heart to them.
34.7: For dreams have led many astray: And they have failed by putting their hope in them.
34.8: Without lying shall the law be accomplished; And wisdom is perfection to a faithful mouth.
34.9: A well-instructed man knows many things; And he that has much experience will declare understanding.
34.10: He that has no experience knows few things: But he that has wandered shall increase his skill.
34.11: In my wandering I have seen many things; And more than my words is my understanding.
34.12: Ofttimes was I in danger even to death; And I was preserved because of these things.
34.13: The spirit of those that fear the Lord shall live; For their hope is upon him that saves them.
34.14: Whoso fears the Lord shall not be afraid, and shall not play the coward; For he is his hope.
34.15: Blessed is the soul of him that fears the Lord: To whom does he give heed? and who is his stay?
34.16: The eyes of the Lord are upon those who love him, A mighty protection and strong stay, A cover from the hot blast, and a cover from the noonday, A guard from stumbling, and a succour from falling.
34.17: He raises up the soul, and enlighteneth the eyes: He gives healing, life, and blessing.
34.18: He that sacrifices of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is made in mockery; And the mockeries of wicked men are not well-pleasing.
34.19: The Most High has no pleasure in the offerings of the ungodly; Neither is he pacified for sins by the multitude of sacrifices.
34.20: As one that kills the son before his father’s eyes Is he that brings a sacrifice from the goods of the poor.
34.21: The bread of the needy is the life of the poor: He that depriveth him thereof is a man of blood.
34.22: As one that slays his neighbor is he that takes away his living; And as a shedder of blood is he that depriveth a hireling of his hire.
34.23: One building, and another pulling down, What profit have they had but toil?
34.24: One praying, and another cursing, Whose voice will the Lord listen to?
34.25: He that washes himself after touching a dead body, and touches it again, What profit has he in his washing?
34.26: Even so a man fasting for his sins, And going again, and doing the same; Who will listen to his prayer? And what profit has he in his humiliation?

35.1: He that keeps the law multiplies offerings; He that takes heed to the commandments sacrifices a peace offering.
35.2: He that requites a good turn offers fine flour; And he that gives alms sacrifices a thank offering.
35.3: To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord; And to depart from unrighteousness is an atoning sacrifice.
35.4: See that you appear not in the presence of the Lord empty.
35.5: For all these things are to be done because of the commandment.
35.6: The offering of the righteous makes the altar fat; And the sweet savor thereof is before the Most High.
35.7: The sacrifice of a righteous man is acceptable; And the memorial thereof shall not be forgotten.
35.8: Glorify the Lord with a good eye, And stint not the first fruits of your hands.
35.9: In every gift show a cheerful countenance, And dedicate your tithe with gladness.
35.10: Give to the Most High according as he has given; And as your hand has found, give with a good eye.
35.11: For the Lord recompenses, And he will recompense you sevenfold.
35.12: Think not to corrupt with gifts; for he will not receive them: And set not your mind on an unrighteous sacrifice; For the Lord is judge, And with him is no respect of persons.
35.13: He will not accept any person against a poor man; And he will listen to the prayer of him that is wronged.
35.14: He will in no wise despise the supplication of the fatherless; Nor the widow, when she pours out her tale.
35.15: Do not the tears of the widow run down her cheek? And is not her cry against him that has caused them to fall?
35.16: He that serves God according to his good pleasure shall be accepted, And his supplication shall reach to the clouds.
35.17: The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds; And till it come near, he will not be comforted; And he will not depart, till the Most High shall visit; And he shall judge righteously, and execute judgement.
35.18: And the Lord will not be slack, neither will he be longsuffering toward them, Till he have crushed the loins of the unmerciful; And he shall repay vengeance to the heathen; Till he have taken away the multitude of the haughty, And broken in pieces the sceptres of the unrighteous;
35.19: Till he have rendered to every man according to his doings, And to the works of men according to their plans; Till he have judged the cause of his people; And he shall make them to rejoice in his mercy.
35.20: Mercy is seasonable in the time of his afflicting them, As clouds of rain in the time of drought.

36.1: Have mercy upon us, O Lord the God of all, and behold;
36.2: And send your fear upon all the nations:
36.3: Lift up your hand against the strange nations; And let them see your mighty power.
36.4: As you were sanctified in us before them, So be you magnified in them before us.
36.5: And let them know you, as we also have known you, That there is no God but only you, O God.
36.6: Show new signs, and work various wonders; Glorify your hand and your right arm.
36.7: Raise up indignation, and pour out wrath; Take away the adversary, and destroy the enemy.
36.8: Hasten the time, and remember the oath; And let them declare your mighty works.
36.9: Let him that escapes be devoured by the rage of fire; And may those who harm your people find destruction.
36.10: Crush the heads of the rulers of the enemies, That say, There is none but we.
36.11: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, And take them for your inheritance, as from the beginning.
36.12: O Lord, have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, And upon Israel, whom you did liken to a firstborn.
36.13: Have compassion upon the city of your sanctuary, Jerusalem, the place of your rest.
36.14: Fill Sion; exalt your oracles, And fill your people with your glory.
36.15: Give testimony to those that were your creatures in the beginning, And raise up the prophecies that have been in your name.
36.16: Give reward to those who wait for you: And men shall put their trust in your prophets.
36.17: Hearken, O Lord, to the prayer of your suppliants, According to the blessing of Aaron concerning your people; And all those who are on the earth shall know That you are the Lord, the eternal God.
36.18: The belly will eat any meat; Yet is one meat better than another.
36.19: The mouth tastes meats taken in hunting: So does an understanding heart false speeches.
36.20: A froward heart will cause heaviness: And a man of experience will recompense him.
36.21: A woman will receive any man; But one daughter is better than another.
36.22: The beauty of a woman cheers the countenance; And a man desires nothing so much.
36.23: If there is on her tongue mercy and meekness, Her husband is not like the sons of men.
36.24: He that gets a wife enters upon a possession: A help meet for him, and a pillar of rest.
36.25: Where no hedge is, the possession will be laid waste: And he that has no wife will mourn as he wandereth up and down.
36.26: For who will trust a nimble robber, that skips from city to city? Even so who shall trust a man that has no nest, and lodges wherever he finds himself at nightfall?

37.1: Every friend will say, I also am his friend: But there is a friend, which is only a friend in name.
37.2: Is there not a grief in it even to death, When a companion and friend is turned to enmity?
37.3: O wicked imagination, whence came you rolling in To cover the dry land with deceitfulness?
37.4: There is a companion, which rejoices in the gladness of a friend, But in time of affliction will be against him.
37.5: There is a companion, which for the belly’s sake labores with his friend, In the face of battle will take up the buckler.
37.6: Forget not a friend in your soul; And be not unmindful of him in your riches.
37.7: Every counsellor extols counsel; But there is that counsels for himself.
37.8: Let your soul beware of a counsellor, And know you before what is his interest (For he will take counsel for himself); Lest he cast the lot upon you,
37.9: And say to you, Your way is good: And he will stand near you, to see what will happen to you.
37.10: Take not counsel with one that looks askance at you; And hide your counsel from such as are jealous of you.
37.11: Take not counsel with a woman about her rival; Neither with a coward about war; Nor with a merchant about exchange; Nor with a buyer about selling; Nor with an envious man about thankfulness; Nor with an unmerciful man about kindliness; Nor with a sluggard about any kind of work; Nor with a hireling in your house about finishing his work; Nor with an idle servant about much business: Give not heed to these in any matter of counsel.
37.12: But rather be continually with a godly man, Whom you shall have known to be a keeper of the commandments, Who in his soul is as your own soul, And who will grieve with you, if you shall miscarry.
37.13: And make the counsel of your heart to stand; For there is none more faithful to you than it.
37.14: For a man’s soul is sometime wont to bring him tidings, More than seven watchmen that sit on high on a watch-tower.
37.15: And above all this entreat the Most High, That he may direct your way in truth.
37.16: Let reason be the beginning of every work, And let counsel go before every action.
37.17: As a token of the changing of the heart,
37.18: four manner of things do rise up, Good and evil, life and death; And that which rules over them continually is the tongue.
37.19: There is one that is shrewd and the instructor of many, And yet is unprofitable to his own soul.
37.20: There is one that is subtle in words, and is hated; He shall be destitute of all food:
37.21: For grace was not given him from the Lord; Because he is deprived of all wisdom.
37.22: There is one that is wise to his own soul; And the fruits of his understanding are trustworthy in the mouth.
37.23: A wise man will instruct his own people; And the fruits of his understanding are trustworthy.
37.24: A wise man shall be filled with blessing; And all those who see him shall call him happy.
37.25: The life of man is counted by days; And the days of Israel are innumerable.
37.26: The wise man shall inherit confidence among his people, And his name shall live forever.
37.27: My son, prove your soul in your life, And see what is evil for it, and give not that to it.
37.28: For all things are not profitable for all men, Neither has every soul pleasure in every thing.
37.29: Be not insatiable in any luxury, And be not greedy on the things that you eatest.
37.30: For in multitude of meats there shall be disease, And surfeiting shall come near to colic.
37.31: Because of surfeiting have many perished; But he that takes heed shall prolong his life.

38.1: Honor a physician according to your need of him with the honors due to him: For verily the Lord has created him.
38.2: For from the Most High comes healing; And from the king he shall receive a gift.
38.3: The skill of the physician shall lift up his head; And in the sight of great men he shall be admired.
38.4: The Lord created medicines out of the earth; And a prudent man will have no disgust at them.
38.5: Was not water made sweet with wood, That the virtue thereof might be known?
38.6: And he gave men skill, That they might be glorified in his marvelous works.
38.7: With them does he heal a man, And takes away his pain.
38.8: With these will the apothecary make a confection; And his works shall not be brought to an end; And from him is peace upon the face of the earth.
38.9: My son, in your sickness be not negligent; But pray to the Lord, and he shall heal you.
38.10: Put away wrong doing, and order your hands aright, And cleanse your heart from all manner of sin.
38.11: Give a sweet savor, and a memorial of fine flour; And make fat your offering, as one that is not.
38.12: Then give place to the physician, for verily the Lord has created him; And let him not go from you, for you have need of him.
38.13: There is a time when in their very hands is the issue for good.
38.14: For they also shall beseech the Lord, That he may prosper them in giving relief and in healing for the maintenance of life.
38.15: He that sins before his Maker, Let him fall into the hands of the physician.
38.16: My son, let your tears fall over the dead, And as one that suffers grievously begin lamentation; And wind up his body according to his due, And neglect not his burial.
38.17: Make bitter weeping, and make passionate wailing, And let your mourning be according to his desert, For one day or two, lest you be evil spoken of: And so be comforted for your sorrow.
38.18: For of sorrow comes death, And sorrow of heart will bow down the strength.
38.19: In calamity sorrow also remains: And the poor man’s life is grievous to the heart.
38.20: Give not your heart to sorrow: Put it away, remembering the last end:
38.21: Forget it not, for there is no returning again: Him you shall not profit, and you will hurt yourself.
38.22: Remember the sentence upon him; for so also shall your be; Yesterday for me, and today for you.
38.23: When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest; And be comforted for him, when his spirit departs from him.
38.24: The wisdom of the scribe comes by opportunity of leisure; And he that has little business shall become wise.
38.25: How shall he become wise that holds the plow, That glories in the shaft of the goad, That drives oxen, and is occupied in their labors, And whose discourse is of the stock of bulls?
38.26: He will set his heart upon turning his furrows; And his wakefulness is to give his heifers their fodder.
38.27: So is every craftsman and workmaster, That passes his time by night as by day; They that cut gravings of signets, And his diligence is to make great variety; He will set his heart to preserve likeness in his portraiture, And will be wakeful to finish his work.
38.28: So is the smith sitting by the anvil, And considering the unwrought iron: The vapor of the fire will waste his flesh; And in the heat of the furnace will he wrestle with his work: The noise of the hammer will be ever in his ear, And his eyes are upon the pattern of the vessel; He will set his heart upon perfecting his works, And And he will be wakeful to adorn them perfectly.
38.29: So is the potter sitting at his work, And turning the wheel about with his feet, Who is always anxiously set at his work, And all his handywork is by number;
38.30: He will fashion the clay with his arm, And will bend its strength in front of his feet; He will apply his heart to finish the glazing; And he will be wakeful to make clean the furnace.
38.31: All these put their trust in their hands; And each becomes wise in his own work.
38.32: Without these shall not a city be inhabited, And men shall not sojourn nor walk up and down therein.
38.33: They shall not be sought for in the council of the people, And in the assembly they shall not mount on high; They shall not sit on the seat of the judge, And they shall not understand the covenant of judgement: Neither shall they declare instruction and judgement; And where parables are they shall not be found.
38.34: But they will maintain the fabric of the world; And in the handywork of their craft is their prayer.

39.1: Not so he that has applied his soul, And meditateth in the law of the Most High; He will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients, And will be occupied in prophecies.
39.2: He will keep the discourse of the men of renown, And will enter in amidst the subtleties of parables.
39.3: He will seek out the hidden meaning of proverbs, And be conversant in the dark sayings of parables.
39.4: He will serve among great men, And appear before him that rules: He will travel through the land of strange nations; For he has tried good things and evil among men.
39.5: He will apply his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, And will make supplication before the Most High, And will open his mouth in prayer, And will make supplication for his sins.
39.6: If the great Lord will, He shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: He shall pour forth the words of his wisdom, And in prayer give thanks to the Lord.
39.7: He shall direct his counsel and knowledge, And in his secrets shall he meditate.
39.8: He shall show forth the instruction which he has been taught, And shall glory in the law of the covenant of the Lord.
39.9: Many shall commend his understanding; And so long as the world endures, it shall not be blotted out: His memorial shall not depart, And his name shall live from generation to generation.
39.10: Nations shall declare his wisdom, And the congregation shall tell out his praise.
39.11: If he continue, he shall leave a greater name than a thousand: And if he die, he adds thereto.
39.12: Yet more will I utter, which I have thought upon; And I am filled as the moon at the full.
39.13: Hearken to me, you holy children, And bud forth as a rose growing by a brook of water:
39.14: And give you a sweet savor as frankencense, And put forth flowers as a lily, Spread abroad a sweet smell, and sing a song of praise; Bless you the Lord for all his works.
39.15: Magnify his name, And give utterance to his praise With the songs of your lips, and with harps; And thus shall you say when you utter his praise:
39.16: All the works of the Lord are exceeding good, And every command shall be accomplished in his season.
39.17: None can say, What is this? wherefore is that? For in his season they shall all be sought out. At his word the waters stood as a heap, And the receptacles of waters at the word of his mouth.
39.18: At his command is all his good pleasure done; And there is none that shall hinder his salvation.
39.19: The works of all flesh are before him; And it is not possible to be hid from his eyes.
39.20: He sees from everlasting to everlasting; And there is nothing wonderful before him.
39.21: None can say, What is this? wherefore is that? For all things are created for their uses.
39.22: His blessing covered the dry land as a river, And saturated it as a flood.
39.23: As he has turned the waters into saltness; So shall the heathen inherit his wrath.
39.24: His ways are plain to the holy; So are they stumbling blocks to the wicked.
39.25: Good things are created from the beginning for the good; So are evil things for sinners.
39.26: The chief of all things necessary for the life of man Are water, and fire, and iron, and salt, And flour of wheat, and honey, and milk, The blood of the grape, and oil, and clothing.
39.27: All these things are for good to the godly; So to the sinners they shall be turned into evil.
39.28: There be winds that are created for vengeance, And in their fury lay on their scourges heavily; In the time of consummation they pour out their strength, And shall appease the wrath of him that made them.
39.29: Fire, and hail, and famine, and death, All these are created for vengeance;
39.30: Teeth of wild beasts, and scorpions and adders, And a sword punishing the ungodly to destruction.
39.31: They shall rejoice in his commandment, And shall be made ready upon earth, when need is; And in their seasons they shall not transgress his word.
39.32: Therefore from the beginning I was resolved, And I thought this, and left it in writing;
39.33: All the works of the Lord are good: And he will supply every need in its season.
39.34: And none can say, This is worse than that: For they shall all be well approved in their season.
39.35: And now with all your heart and mouth sing you praises, And bless the name of the Lord.

40.1: Great travail is created for every man, And a heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam, From the day of their coming forth from their mother’s womb, Until the day for their burial in the mother of all things.
40.2: The expectation of things to come, and the day of death, Trouble their thoughts, and cause fear of heart;
40.3: From him that sits on a throne of glory, Even to him that is humbled in earth and ashes;
40.4: From him that wears purple and a crown, Even to him that is clothed with a hempen frock.
40.5: There is wrath, and jealousy, and trouble, and disquiet, And fear of death, and anger, and strife; And in the time of rest upon his bed His night sleep does change his knowledge.
40.6: A little or nothing is his resting, And afterward in his sleep, as in a day of keeping watch, He is troubled in the vision of his heart, As one that has escaped from the front of battle.
40.7: In the very time of his deliverance he awakens, And marvels that the fear is nothing.
40.8: It is thus with all flesh, from man to beast, And upon sinners sevenfold more.
40.9: Death, and bloodshed, and strife, and sword, Calamities, famine, tribulation, and the scourge;
40.10: All these things were created for the wicked, And because of them came the flood.
40.11: All things that are of the earth turn to the earth again: And all things that are of the waters return into the sea.
40.12: All bribery and injustice shall be blotted out; And good faith shall stand forever.
40.13: The goods of the unjust shall be dried up like a river, And like a great thunder in rain shall go off in noise.
40.14: In opening his hands a man shall be made glad: So shall transgressors utterly fail.
40.15: The children of the ungodly shall not put forth many branches; And are as unclean roots upon a sheer rock.
40.16: The sedge that grows upon every water and bank of a river Shall be plucked up before all grass.
40.17: Bounty is as a garden of blessings, And almsgiving endures forever.
40.18: The life of one that labores, and is contented, shall be made sweet; And he that finds a treasure is above both.
40.19: Children and the building of a city establish a man’s name; And a blameless wife is counted above both.
40.20: Wine and music rejoice the heart; And the love of wisdom is above both.
40.21: The pipe and the lute make pleasant melody; And a pleasant tongue is above both.
40.22: Your eye shall desire grace and beauty; And above both the green blade of corn.
40.23: A friend and a companion never meet amiss; And a wife with her husband is above both.
40.24: Brethren and succour are for a time of affliction; And almsgiving is a deliverer above both.
40.25: Gold and silver will make the foot stand sure; And counsel is esteemed above them both.
40.26: Riches and strength will lift up the heart; And the fear of the Lord is above both: There is nothing lacking in the fear of the Lord, And there is no need to seek help therein.
40.27: The fear of the Lord is as a garden of blessing, And covers a man above all glory.
40.28: My son, lead not a beggar’s life; Better it is to die than to beg.
40.29: A man that looks to the table of another, His life is not to be counted for a life; He will pollute his soul with another man’s meats: But a man wise and well-instructed will beware thereof.
40.30: In the mouth of the shameless begging will be sweet; And in his belly a fire shall be kindled.

41.1: O death, how bitter is the remembrance of you to a man that is at peace in his possessions, To the man that has nothing to distract him, and has prosperity in all things, And that still has strength to receive meat!
41.2: O death, acceptable is your sentence to a man that is needy, and that fails in strength, That is in extreme old age, and is distracted about all things, And is perverse, and has lost patience!
41.3: Don’t be afraid of the sentence of death; Remember those who have been before you, and that come after: This is the sentence from the Lord over all flesh.
41.4: And why do you refuse, when it is the good pleasure of the Most High? Whether it be ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years, There is no inquisition of life in the grave.
41.5: The children of sinners are abominable children, And they frequent the dwellings of the ungodly.
41.6: The inheritance of sinners’ children shall perish, And with their posterity shall be a perpetual reproach.
41.7: Children will complain of an ungodly father, Because they shall be reproached for his sake.
41.8: Woe to you, ungodly men, Which have forsaken the law of the Most High God!
41.9: If you be born, you shall be born to a curse; If you die, a curse shall be your portion.
41.10: All things that are of the earth shall go back to the earth: So the ungodly shall go from a curse to perdition.
41.11: The mourning of men is about their bodies: But the name of sinners being evil shall be blotted out.
41.12: Have regard to your name; For it continueth with you longer than a thousand great treasures of gold.
41.13: A good life has its number of days; And a good name continueth forever.
41.14: My children, keep instruction in peace: But wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seen, What profit is in them both?
41.15: Better is a man that hides his foolishness Than a man that hides his wisdom.
41.16: Wherefore show reverence to my word: For it is not good to retain every kind of shame; And not all things are approved by all in good faith.
41.17: Be ashamed of whoredom before father and mother: And of a lie before a prince and a mighty man;
41.18: Of an offence before a judge and ruler; Of iniquity before the congregation and the people; Of unjust dealing before a partner and friend;
41.19: And of theft in regard of the place where you sojourn, And in regard of the truth of God and his covenant; And of leaning with your elbow at meat; And of scurrility in the matter of giving and taking;
41.20: And of silence before those who salute you; And of looking upon a woman that is a harlot;
41.21: And of turning away your face from a kinsman; Of taking away a portion or a gift; And of gazing upon a woman that has a husband;
41.22: Of being over busy with his maid; and come not near her bed; Of upbraiding speeches before friends; And after you have given, upbraid not;
41.23: Of repeating and speaking what you have heard; And of revealing of secrets.
41.24: So shall you be truly shamefast, And find favor in the sight of every man.

42.1: Of these things be not ashamed, And accept no man’s person to sin thereby:
42.2: Of the law of the Most High, and his covenant; And of judgement to do justice to the ungodly;
42.3: Of reckoning with a partner and with travellers; And of a gift from the heritage of friends;
42.4: Of exactness of balance and weights; And of getting much or little;
42.5: Of indifferent selling of merchants; And of much correction of children; And of making the side of an evil servant to bleed.
42.6: Sure keeping is good, where an evil wife is; And where many hands are, shut you close.
42.7: Whatsoever you handest over, let it be by number and weight; And in giving and receiving let all be in writing.
42.8: Be not ashamed to instruct the unwise and foolish, And one of extreme old age that contends with those that are young; And so shall you be well instructed indeed, And approved in the sight of every man living.
42.9: A daughter is a secret cause of wakefulness to a father; And the care for her puts away sleep; In her youth, lest she pass the flower of her age; And when she is married, lest she should be hated:
42.10: In her virginity, lest she should be defiled And be with child in her father’s house; And when she has a husband, lest she should transgress; And when she is married, lest she should be barren.
42.11: Keep a strict watch over a headstrong daughter, Lest she make you a laughing stock to your enemies, A byword in the city and notorious among the people, And shame you before the multitude.
42.12: Look not upon every body in regard of beauty, And sit not in the midst of women;
42.13: For from garments comes a moth, And from a woman a woman’s wickedness.
42.14: Better is the wickedness of a man than a pleasant-dealing woman, And a woman which puts you to shameful reproach.
42.15: I will make mention now of the works of the Lord, And will declare the things that I have seen: In the words of the Lord are his works.
42.16: The sun that gives light looks upon all things; And the work of the Lord is full of his glory.
42.17: The Lord has not given power to the saints to declare all his marvelous works; Which the Almighty Lord firmly settled, That whatever is might be established in his glory.
42.18: He searcheth out the deep, and the heart, And he has understanding of their cunning plans: For the Most High knows all knowledge, And he looks into the signs of the world,
42.19: Declaring the things that are past, and the things that shall be, And revealing the traces of hidden things.
42.20: No thought escapes him; There is not a word hid from him.
42.21: The mighty works of his wisdom he has ordered, Who is from everlasting to everlasting: Nothing has been added to them, nor diminished from them; And he had no need of any counsellor.
42.22: How desirable are all his works! One may behold this even to a spark.
42.23: All these things live and remain forever in all manner of uses, And they are all obedient.
42.24: All things are double one against another: And he has made nothing imperfect.
42.25: One thing establishes the good things of another: And who shall be filled with beholding his glory?

43.1: The pride of the height is the firmament in its clearness, The appearance of heaven, in the spectacle of its glory.
43.2: The sun when he appears, bringing tidings as he goes forth, Is a marvelous instrument, the work of the Most High:
43.3: At his noon he dries up the country, And who shall stand against his burning heat?
43.4: A man blowing a furnace is in works of heat, But the sun three times more, burning up the mountains: Breathing out fiery vapours, And sending forth bright beams, he dims the eyes.
43.5: Great is the Lord that made him; And at his word he hastens his course.
43.6: The moon also is in all things for her season, For a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.
43.7: From the moon is the sign of the feast day; A light that waneth when she is come to the full.
43.8: The month is called after her name, Increasing wonderfully in her changing; An instrument of the army on high, Shining forth in the firmament of heaven;
43.9: The beauty of heaven, the glory of the stars, An ornament giving light in the highest places of the Lord.
43.10: At the word of the Holy One they will stand in due order, And they will not faint in their watches.
43.11: Look upon the rainbow, and praise him that made it; Exceeding beautiful in the brightness thereof.
43.12: It encircles the heaven round about with a circle of glory; The hands of the Most High have stretched it.
43.13: By his commandment he makes the snow to fall apace, And sends swiftly the lightnings of his judgement.
43.14: By reason thereof the treasure-houses are opened; And clouds fly forth as fowls.
43.15: By his mighty power he makes strong the clouds, And the hailstones are broken small:
43.16: And at his appearing the mountains will be shaken, And at his will the south wind will blow.
43.17: The voice of his thunder makes the earth to travail; So does the northern storm and the whirlwind: As birds flying down he sprinkleth the snow; And as the lighting of the locust is the falling down thereof:
43.18: The eye will marvel at the beauty of its whiteness, And the heart will be astonished at the raining of it.
43.19: The hoar frost also he pours on the earth as salt; And when it is congealed, it is as points of thorns.
43.20: The cold north wind shall blow, And the ice shall be congealed on the water: It shall lodge upon every gathering together of water, And the water shall put on as it were a breastplate.
43.21: It shall devour the mountains, and burn up the wilderness, And consume the green herb as fire.
43.22: A mist coming speedily is the healing of all things; A dew coming after heat shall bring cheerfulness.
43.23: By his counsel he has stilled the deep, And planted islands therein.
43.24: They that sail on the sea tell of the danger thereof; And when we hear it with our ears, we marvel.
43.25: Therein be also those strange and wondrous works, Variety of all that has life, the race of sea-monsters.
43.26: By reason of him his end has success, And by his word all things consist.
43.27: We may say many things, yet shall we not attain; And the sum of our words is, He is all.
43.28: How shall we have strength to glorify him? For he is himself the great one above all his works.
43.29: The Lord is terrible and exceeding great; And marvelous is his power.
43.30: When you glorify the Lord, exalt him as much as you can; For even yet will he exceed: And when you exalt him, put forth your full strength: Be not weary; for you will never attain.
43.31: Who has seen him, that he may declare him? And who shall magnify him as he is?
43.32: Many things are hidden greater than these; For we have seen but a few of his works.
43.33: For the Lord made all things; And to the godly gave he wisdom.

44.1: Let us now praise famous men, And our fathers that became the father of us.
44.2: The Lord manifested in them great glory, Even his mighty power from the beginning.
44.3: Such as did bear rule in their kingdoms, And were men renowned for their power, Giving counsel by their understanding, Such as have brought tidings in prophecies:
44.4: Leaders of the people by their counsels, And by their understanding men of learning for the people; Wise were their words in their instruction:
44.5: Such as sought out musical tunes, And set forth verses in writing:
44.6: Rich men furnished with ability, Living peaceably in their habitations:
44.7: All these were honored in their generations, And were a glory in their days.
44.8: There be of them, that have left a name behind them, To declare their praises.
44.9: And some there be, which have no memorial; Who are perished as though they had not been, And are become as though they had not been born; And their children after them.
44.10: But these were men of mercy, Whose righteous deeds have not been forgotten.
44.11: With their seed shall remain continually a good inheritance; Their children are within the covenants.
44.12: Their seed stands fast, And their children for their sakes.
44.13: Their seed shall remain forever, And their glory shall not be blotted out.
44.14: Their bodies were buried in peace, And their name lives to all generations.
44.15: Peoples will declare their wisdom, And the congregation tells out their praise.
44.16: Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, Being an example of repentance to all generations.
44.17: Noah was found perfect and righteous; In the season of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world; Therefore was there left a remnant to the earth, When the flood came.
44.18: Everlasting covenants were made with him, That all flesh should no more be blotted out by a flood.
44.19: Abraham was a great father of a multitude of nations; And there was none found like him in glory;
44.20: Who kept the law of the Most High, And was taken into covenant with him: In his flesh he established the covenant; And when he was proved, he was found faithful.
44.21: Therefore he assured him by an oath, That the nations should be blessed in his seed; That he would multiply him as the dust of the earth, And exalt his seed as the stars, And cause them to inherit from sea to sea, And from the River to the utmost part of the earth.
44.22: In Isaac also did he establish likewise, for Abraham his father’s sake, The blessing of all men, and the covenant:
44.23: And he made it rest upon the head of Jacob; He acknowledged him in his blessings, And gave to him by inheritance, And divided his portions; Among twelve tribes did he part them.

45.1: And he brought out of him a man of mercy, Which found favor in the sight of all flesh; A man beloved of God and men, even Moses, Whose memorial is blessed.
45.2: He made him like to the glory of the saints, And magnified him in the fears of his enemies.
45.3: By his words he caused the wonders to cease; He glorified him in the sight of kings; He gave him commandment for his people, And showed him part of his glory.
45.4: He sanctified him in his faithfulness and meekness; He chose him out of all flesh.
45.5: He made him to hear his voice, And led him into the thick darkness, And gave him commandments face to face, Even the law of life and knowledge, That he might teach Jacob the covenant, And Israel his judgments.
45.6: He exalted Aaron, a holy man like to him, Even his brother, of the tribe of Levi.
45.7: He established for him an everlasting covenant, And gave him the priesthood of the people; He beautified him with comely ornaments, And girded him about with a robe of glory.
45.8: He clothed him with the perfection of exultation; And strengthened him with apparel of honor, The linen breeches, the long robe, and the ephod.
45.9: And he compassed him with pomegranates of gold, And with many bells round about, To send forth a sound as he went, To make a sound that might be heard in the temple, For a memorial to the children of his people;
45.10: With a holy garment, with gold and blue and purple, the work of the embroiderer, With an oracle of judgement, even with the Urim and Thummim;
45.11: With twisted scarlet, the work of the craftsman; With precious stones graven like a signet, in a setting of gold, the work of the jeweller, For a memorial engraved in writing, after the number of the tribes of Israel;
45.12: With a crown of gold upon the mitre, having graven on it, as on a signet, HOLINESS, An ornament of honor, a work of might, The desires of the eyes, goodly and beautiful.
45.13: Before him there never have been any such; No stranger put them on, but his sons only, and his offspring perpertually.
45.14: His sacrifices shall be wholly consumed Every day twice continually.
45.15: Moses consecrated him, And anointed him with holy oil: It was to him for an everlasting covenant, And to his seed, all the days of heaven, To minister to him, and to execute also the priest’s office, And bless his people in his name.
45.16: He chose him out of all living To offer sacrifice to the Lord, Incense, and a sweet savor, for a memorial, To make reconciliation for your people.
45.17: He gave to him in his commandments, Yes, authority in the covenants of judgements, To teach Jacob the testimonies, And to enlighten Israel in his law.
45.18: Strangers gathered themselves together against him, And envied him in the wilderness, Even Dathan and Abiram with their company, And the congregation of Korah, with wrath and anger.
45.19: The Lord saw it, and it displeased him; And in the wrath of his anger they were destroyed: He did wonders upon them, To consume them with flaming fire.
45.20: And he added glory to Aaron, And gave him a heritage: He divided to him the first fruits of the increase; And first did he prepare bread in abundance:
45.21: For they shall eat the sacrifices of the Lord, Which he gave to him and to his seed.
45.22: Howbeit in the land of the people he shall have no inheritance, And he has no portion among the people: For he himself is your portion and inheritance.
45.23: And Phinehas the son of Eleazar is the third in glory, In that he was zealous in the fear of the Lord, And stood fast in the good forwardness of his soul when the people turned away, And he made reconciliation for Israel.
45.24: Therefore was there a covenant of peace established for him, That he should be leader of the saints and of his people; That he and his seed Should have the dignity of the priesthood forever.
45.25: Also he made a covenant with David the son of Jesse, of the tribe of Judah; The inheritance of the king is his alone from son to son; So the inheritance of Aaron is also to his seed.
45.26: God give you wisdom in your heart To judge his people in righteousness, That their good things be not abolished, And that their glory endure for all their generations.

46.1: Joshua the son of Nun was valiant in war, And was the successor of Moses in prophecies: Who according to his name was made great For the saving of God’s elect, To take vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them, That he might give Israel their inheritance.
46.2: How was he glorified in the lifting up his hands, And in stretching out his sword against the cities!
46.3: Who before him so stood fast? For the Lord himself brought his enemies to him.
46.4: Did not the sun go back by his hand? And did not one day become as two?
46.5: He called upon the Most High and Mighty One, When his foes pressed him round about; And the great Lord heard him.
46.6: With hailstones of mighty power He caused war to break violently upon the nation, And in the going down he destroyed those who resisted; That the nations might know his armor, How that he fought in the sight of the Lord; For he followed after the Mighty One.
46.7: Also in the time of Moses he did a work of mercy, He and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, In that they withstood the adversary, Hindered the people from sin, And stilled the murmuring of wickedness.
46.8: And of six hundred thousand people on foot, they two alone were preserved To bring them into the heritage, Even into a land flowing with milk and honey.
46.9: Also the Lord gave strength to Caleb, And it remained with him to his old age; So that he entered upon the height of the land, And his seed obtained it for a heritage:
46.10: That all the children of Israel might see That it is good to walk after the Lord.
46.11: Also the judges, every one by his name, All whose hearts went not a whoring, And who turned not away from the Lord, May their memorial be blessed.
46.12: May their bones flourish again out of their place, And may the name of those who have been honored be renewed upon their children.
46.13: Samuel, the prophet of the Lord, beloved of his Lord, Established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people.
46.14: By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, And the Lord visited Jacob.
46.15: By his faithfulness he was proved to be a prophet, And by his words he was known to be faithful in vision.
46.16: Also when his enemies pressed him round about He called upon the Lord, the Mighty One, With the offering of the sucking lamb.
46.17: And the Lord thundered from heaven, And with a mighty sound made his voice to be heard.
46.18: And he utterly destroyed the rulers of the Tyrians, And all the princes of the Philistines.
46.19: Also before the time of his long sleep He made protestations in the sight of the lord and his anointed, I have not taken any man’s goods, so much as a shoe: And no man did accuse him.
46.20: And after he fell asleep he prophesied, And showed the king his end, And lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy, To blot out the wickedness of the people.

47.1: And after him rose up Nathan To prophesy in the days of David.
47.2: As is the fat when it is separated from the peace offering, So was David separated from the children of Israel.
47.3: He played with lions as with kids, And with bears as with lambs of the flock.
47.4: In his youth did he not kill a giant, And take away reproach from the people, When he lifted up his hand with a sling stone, And beat down the boasting of Goliath?
47.5: For he called upon the Most High Lord; And he gave him strength in his right hand, To kill a man mighty in war, To exalt the horn of his people.
47.6: So they glorified him for his ten thousands, And praised him for the blessings of the Lord, In that there was given him a diadem of glory.
47.7: For he destroyed the enemies on every side, And brought to nothing the Philistines his adversaries, Brake their horn in pieces to this day.
47.8: In every work of his he gave thanks to the Holy One Most High with words of glory; With his whole heart he sang praise, And loved him that made him.
47.9: Also he set singers before the altar, And to make sweet melody by their music.
47.10: He gave comeliness to the feasts, And set in order the seasons to perfection, While they praised his holy name, And the sanctuary sounded from early morning.
47.11: The Lord took away his sins, And exalted his horn forever; And gave him a covenant of kings, And a throne of glory in Israel.
47.12: After him rose up a son, a man of understanding; And for his sake he lived at large.
47.13: Solomon reigned in days of peace; And to him God gave rest round about, That he might set up a house for his name, And prepare a sanctuary forever.
47.14: How wise was you made in your youth, And filled as a river with understanding!
47.15: Your soul covered the earth, And you filled it with dark parables.
47.16: Your name reached to the aisles afar off; And for your peace you were beloved.
47.17: For your songs and proverbs and parables, And for your interpretations, the countries marveled at you.
47.18: By the name of the Lord God, Which is called the God of Israel, You did gather gold as tin, And did multiply silver as lead.
47.19: You did bow your loins to women, And in your body you were brought into subjection.
47.20: You did blemish your honor, And profane your seed, To bring wrath upon your children; And I was grieved for your folly:
47.21: So that the sovereignty was divided, And out of Ephraim ruled a disobedient kingdom.
47.22: But the Lord will never forsake his mercy; And he will not destroy any of his works, Nor blot out the posterity of his elect; And the seed of him that loved him he will not take away; And he gave a remnant to Jacob, And to David a root out of him.
47.23: And so rested Solomon with his fathers; And of his seed he left behind him Rehoboam, Even the foolishness of the people, and one that lacked understanding, Who made the people to revolt by his counsel. Also Jeroboam the son of Nebat, Who made Israel to sin, And gave to Ephraim a way of sin.
47.24: And their sins were multiplied exceedingly, To remove them from their land.
47.25: For they sought out all manner of wickedness, Till vengeance should come upon them.

48.1: Also there arose Elijah the prophet as fire, And his word burned like a torch:
48.2: Who brought a famine upon them, And by his zeal made them few in number.
48.3: By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven: Thrice did he thus bring down fire.
48.4: How was you glorified, O Elijah, in your wondrous deeds! And who shall glory like to you?
48.5: Who did raise up a dead man from death, And from the place of the dead, by the word of the Most High:
48.6: Who brought down kings to destruction, And honorable men from their bed:
48.7: Who heard rebuke in Sinai, And judgements of vengeance in Horeb:
48.8: Who anointed kings for retribution, And prophets to succeed after him:
48.9: Who was taken up in a tempest of fire, In a chariot of fiery horses:
48.10: Who was recorded for reproofs in their seasons, To pacify anger, before it brake forth into wrath; To turn the heart of the father to the son, And to restore the tribes of Jacob.
48.11: Blessed are those who saw you, And those who have been beautified with love; For we also shall surely live.
48.12: Elijah it was, who was wrapped in a tempest: And Elisha was filled with his spirit; And in all his days he was not moved by the fear of any ruler, And no one brought him into subjection.
48.13: Nothing was too high for him; And when he was laid on sleep his body prophesied.
48.14: As in his life he did wonders, So in death were his works marvelous.
48.15: For all this the people repented not, And they departed not from their sins, Till they were carried away as a plunder from their land, And were scattered through all the earth; And the people was left very few in number, And a ruler was left in the house of David.
48.16: Some of them did that which was pleasing to God, And some multiplied sins.
48.17: Hezekiah fortified his city, And brought in water into the midst of them: He digged the sheer rock with iron, And built up wells for waters.
48.18: In his days Sennacherib came up, And sent Rabshakeh, and departed; And he lifted up his hand against Sion, And boasted great things in his arrogancy.
48.19: Then were their hearts and their hands shaken, And they were in pain, as women in travail;
48.20: And they called upon the Lord which is merciful, Spreading forth their hands to him: And the Holy One heard them speedily out of Heaven, And delivered them by the hand of Isaiah.
48.21: He struck the camp of the Assyrians, And his angel utterly destroyed them.
48.22: For Hezekiah did that which was pleasing to the Lord, And was strong in the ways of David his father, Which Isaiah the prophet commanded, Who was great and faithful in his vision.
48.23: In his days the sun went backward; And he added life to the king.
48.24: He saw by an excellent spirit what should come to pass at the last; And he comforted those who mourned in Sion.
48.25: He showed the things that should be to the end of time, And the hidden things or ever they came.

49.1: The memorial of Josiah is like the composition of incense Prepared by the work of the apothecary: It shall be sweet as honey in every mouth, And as music at a banquet of wine.
49.2: He behaved himself uprightly in the conversion of the people, And took away the abominations of iniquity.
49.3: He set his heart right toward the Lord; In the days of wicked men he made godliness to prevail.
49.4: Except David and Hezekiah and Josiah, All committed trespass: For they forsook the law of the Most High; The kings of Judah failed.
49.5: For they gave their power to others, And their glory to a strange nation.
49.6: They set on fire the chosen city of the sanctuary, And made her streets desolate, as it was written by the hand of Jeremiah.
49.7: For they entreated him evil; And yet he was sanctified in the womb to be a prophet, To root out, and to afflict, and to destroy; And in like manner to build and to plant.
49.8: It was Ezekiel who saw the vision of glory, Which God showed him upon the chariot of the cherubim.
49.9: For verily he remembered the enemies in storm, And to do good to those who directed their ways aright.
49.10: Also of the twelve prophets May the bones flourish again out of their place. And he comforted Jacob, And delivered them by confidence of hope.
49.11: How shall we magnify Zerubbabel? And he was as a signet on the right hand:
49.12: So was Jesus the son of Josedek: Who in their days built the house, And exalted a people holy to the Lord, Prepared for everlasting glory.
49.13: Also of Nehemiah the memorial is great; Who raised up for us the walls that were fallen, And set up the gates and bars, And raised up our homes again.
49.14: No man was created upon the earth such as was Enoch; For he was taken up from the earth.
49.15: Neither was there a man born like to Joseph, A governor of his kindred, a stay of the people: Yes, his bones were visited.
49.16: Shem and Seth were glorified among men; And above every living thing in the creation is Adam.

50.1: It was Simon, the son of Onias, the great priest, Who in his life repaired the house, And in his days strengthened the temple:
50.2: And by him was built from the foundation the height of the double wall, The lofty underworks of the inclosure of the temple:
50.3: In his days the cistern of waters was diminished, The brazen vessel in compass as the sea.
50.4: It was he that took thought for his people that they should not fall, And fortified the city against besieging:
50.5: How glorious was he when the people gathered round him At his coming forth out of the sanctuary!
50.6: As the morning star in the midst of a cloud, As the moon at the full:
50.7: As the sun shining forth upon the temple of the Most High, And as the rainbow giving light in clouds of glory:
50.8: As the flower of roses in the days of new fruits, As lilies at the waterspring, As the shoot of the frankencense tree in the time of summer:
50.9: As fire and incense in the censer, As a vessel all of beaten gold Adorned with all manner of precious stones:
50.10: As an olive tree budding forth fruits, And as a cypress growing high among the clouds.
50.11: When he took up the robe of glory, And put on the perfection of exultation, In the ascent of the holy altar, He made glorious the precinct of the sanctuary.
50.12: And when he received the portions out of the priests’ hands, Himself also standing by the hearth of the altar, His kindred as a garland round about him, He was as a young cedar in Libanus; And as stems of palm trees compassed they him round about,
50.13: And all the sons of Aaron in their glory, And the Lord’s offering in their hands, before all the congregation of Israel.
50.14: And finishing the service at the altars, That he might adorn the offering of the Most High, the Almighty,
50.15: He stretched out his hand to the cup, And poured out the cup of the grape; He poured out at the foot of the altar A sweet smelling savor to the Most High, the King of all.
50.16: Then shouted the sons of Aaron, They sounded the trumpets of beaten work, They made a great noise to be heard, For a remembrance before the Most High.
50.17: Then all the people together hurried, And fell down upon the earth on their faces To worship their Lord, the Almighty, God Most High.
50.18: The singers also praised him with their voices; In the whole house was there made sweet melody.
50.19: And the people implored the Lord Most High, In prayer before him that is merciful. Till the worship of the Lord should be ended; And so they accomplished his service.
50.20: Then he went down, and lifted up his hands Over the whole congregation of the children of Israel, To give blessing to the Lord with his lips, And to glory in his name.
50.21: And he bowed himself down in worship the second time, To declare the blessing from the Most High.
50.22: And now bless you the God of all, Which everywhere does great things, Which exalts our days from the womb, And deals with us according to his mercy.
50.23: May he grant us joyfulness of heart, And that peace may be in our days in Israel for the days of eternity:
50.24: To intrust his mercy with us; And let him deliver us in his time!
50.25: With two nations is my soul vexed, And the third is no nation:
50.26: They that sit upon the mountain of Samaria, and the Philistines, And that foolish people that dwells in Sichem.
50.27: I have written in this book the instruction of understanding and knowledge, I Jesus, the son of Sirach Eleazar, of Jerusalem, Who out of his heart poured forth wisdom.
50.28: Blessed is he that shall be exercised in these things; And he that lays them up in his heart shall become wise.
50.29: For if he do them, he shall be strong to all things: For the light of the Lord is his guide.

51.1: I will give thanks to you, O Lord, O King, And will praise you, O God my Saviour: I do give thanks to your name:
51.2: For you were my protector and helper, And did deliver my body out of destruction, And out of the snare of a slanderous tongue, From lips that forge lies, And was my helper before those who stood by;
51.3: And did deliver me, according to the abundance of your mercy, and greatness of your name, From the gnashings of teeth ready to devour, Out of the hand of such as sought my life, Out of the manifold afflictions which I had;
51.4: From the choking of a fire on every side, And out of the midst of fire which I kindled not;
51.5: Out of the depth of the belly of the grave, And from an unclean tongue, And from lying words,
51.6: The slander of an unrighteous tongue to the king. My soul drew near even to death, And my life was near to the grave beneath.
51.7: They compassed me on every side, And there was none to help me. I was looking for the succour of men, And it was not.
51.8: And I remembered your mercy, O Lord, And your working which has been from everlasting, How you deliver those who wait for you, And save them out of the hand of the enemies.
51.9: And I lifted up my supplication from the earth, And prayed for deliverance from death.
51.10: I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, That he would not forsake me in the days of affliction, In the time when there was no help against the proud.
51.11: I will praise your name continually, And will sing praise with thanksgiving; And my supplication was heard:
51.12: For you saved me from destruction, And delivered me from the evil time: Therefore will I give thanks and praise to you, And bless the name of the Lord.
51.13: When I was yet young, Or ever I went abroad, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer.
51.14: Before the temple I asked for her, And I will seek her out even to the end.
51.15: From her flower as from the ripening grape my heart delighted in her: My foot trod in uprightness, From my youth I tracked her out.
51.16: I bowed down my ear a little, and received her, And found for myself much instruction.
51.17: I profited in her: To him that gives me wisdom I will give glory.
51.18: For I purposed to practice her, And I was zealous for that which is good; And I shall never be put to shame.
51.19: My soul has wrestled in her, And in my doing I was exact: I spread forth my hands to the heaven above, And bewailed my ignorances of her.
51.20: I set my soul aright to her, And in pureness I found her. I got me a heart joined with her from the beginning: Therefore shall I not be forsaken.
51.21: My inward part also was troubled to seek her: Therefore I have gotten a good possession.
51.22: The Lord gave me a tongue for my reward; And I will praise him therewith.
51.23: Draw near to me, you unlearned, And lodge in the house of instruction.
51.24: Say, wherefore are you lacking in these things, And your souls are very thirsty?
51.25: I opened my mouth, and spoke, Get her for yourselves without money.
51.26: Put your neck under the yoke, And let your soul receive instruction: She is hard at hand to find.
51.27: Behold with your eyes, How that I laboured but a little, And found for myself much rest.
51.28: Get you instruction with a great sum of silver, And gain much gold by her.
51.29: May your soul rejoice in his mercy, And may you not be put to shame in praising him.
51.30: Work your work before the time comes, And in his time he will give you your reward.

quotes.quote: Therefore, let us always walk as if in the day, and let us cast off the works of darkness. For we know that night is given for the rest of the body, not for the pursuit of any task or work, which is passed in sleep and oblivion. Let there not be among us revelry, drunkenness, debauchery. Let us not say: Darkness and walls cover us, and who knows if the Most High will see? But let there be among us a love of light and a care for honesty, so that as if walking in daylight, we may desire our works to shine before God, to whom be honor, praise, and glory, perpetuity from age to age, now and forever, and for all ages of ages. Amen.

But God, who knew that wine consumed in moderation would bring health and increase wisdom, and that excessive consumption would lead to vices, created the substance and left its abundance to human discretion. This way, the moderation of nature would serve as a lesson in sobriety, and the harmful consequences of excess would be attributed to human choice. In fact, even Noah himself became intoxicated and fell asleep as a result of wine. And so, through wine, the deformity that arose from the flood became evident to glory: but the Lord also reserved his grace in it, so that he might convert its fruit for our salvation, and through it forgiveness of sins might come to us.

"He who is called in the Lord as a slave is a freedman of the Lord." Someone who is rescued from sins, which are truly indicative of "slaves," becomes a freedman of the Lord. For he who behaves unwisely is a slave through and through. This was the opinion of the ancients too, who called wise people "free," and all the unwise, "slaves." Thus Solomon says, "Free people shall serve a slave who is wise." Therefore one who believes, even if he is a slave for a time, becomes a freedman of the Lord because, in believing in Christ, he is doing a wise thing. For sins create slaves, as Ham the son of Noah was made a slave for his sin and lack of prudence, for when someone receives remission of sins, he becomes a freedman.
quotes.source_title: COMMENTARY ON THE FIRST LETTER TO THE CORINTHIANS 7:22.1

quotes.quote: HOW IS IT THAT THE SAME SOLOMON SAYS, “GOD,” HE DECLARES, “DID NOT MAKE DEATH,” WHILE IN ANOTHER PLACE HE SAYS, “GOOD THINGS AND EVIL, LIFE AND DEATH, POVERTY AND RICHES ARE FROM GOD” (Wisdom 1:13; Sirach 11:14)? There is no doubt that all good things are from God, but the “evils” he mentioned are evils only in that God is avenging himself on us. For even though punishment is justly inflicted, it still seems an evil to the one who suffers it. Therefore God speaks through the prophet to sinners, saying, “I will bring evils upon you,” that is, “I will deal with you by punishments.” Life and death are from God in this way: he gave a law which promises life to those who keep it, but death to those who reject it, yet that death which is called the second death. For when he judges each person according to what he deserves, it is from him, whether it be freeing leading to life or guilt leading…
quotes.source_title: QUESTIONS ON THE OLD AND NEW TESTAMENTS, QUESTION 34: GOD DID NOT MAKE DEATH, YET DEATH IS FROM GOD

quotes.quote: WHY DOES SOLOMON SAY, "JUSTIFY YOUR SOUL BEFORE YOUR DEATH," AS WE READ IN A PSALM, "NO LIVING MAN WILL BE JUSTIFIED IN YOUR PRESENCE?" —A person justifies his soul before death when, through hope of future life, he reaches faith, so that he may not die in transgression. But Solomon is speaking of someone who lives under the Law and does not conduct himself justly. If such a person corrects his mind so as to walk in the paths of righteousness, he justifies his soul before death. For Solomon, because of the coming judgment, has given this advice, lest anyone careless about himself should die in his sins. David, however, spoke about the perfection of righteousness: for no one will be justified before God so as to be worthy of the promise, unless he has died in righteousness. As long as a person lives, he does not yet possess the full merit of what is to come. Therefore the Savior says,…
quotes.source_title: QUESTIONS ON THE OLD AND NEW TESTAMENTS, QUESTION 22: JUSTIFY YOUR SOUL BEFORE YOUR DEATH

quotes.quote: This most celebrated Virgin was of David's seed, from which her husband also drew his descent. In fact, according to the great apostle, "Man is the head of the woman," and, according to Moses law, "The two shall become one flesh." And if the married woman who has offended her husband pays the punishment for adultery according to the Law—as by now she has become the body of the husband and has chosen the man as her head—how, then, does it not follow that, once the genealogy of the head is traced, the body is also counted together with the head? As a consequence it was also necessary in this case that the Virgin, being united with Joseph, was conveniently included in his genealogy, just as we have demonstrated that she was born of the same tribe as he—yes, from the very clan and family of David. And therefore also Gabriel foretold in the prophecy addressed to her, among other things: "And…

Therefore, although wicked people press forward to keep the feast and praise God as though they were at a feast and intrude into the church of the saints, yet God confutes them, saying to the sinner, "Why do you speak of my decrees?" And the gentle Spirit rebukes them, saying, "Praise is not attractive in the mouth of sinners," neither does sin have anything in common with the praise of God; for the sinner has a mouth speaking perverse things, as the proverb says, "The mouth of the wicked answers evil." For how is it possible for us to praise God with an impure mouth, since things that are contrary to each other cannot coexist? "For what communion has righteousness with iniquity, or what fellowship is there between light and darkness?" So exclaims Paul, a minister of the gospel. Thus it is that sinners, and all those who have alienated themselves from the catholic church, heretics and…

Sin possesses the very bread of his death, to which it invites those who love pleasures and the fools, saying, "Touch with pleasure the secret bread and the sweet stolen waters." He who merely touches it "does not know that the children of the earth perish because of it." When one thinks about tasting pleasure, the result that comes from this nourishment will not be sweet for him in the end, as again the Wisdom of God affirms: "Bread of deceit is pleasant to a person, but afterwards his mouth shall be full of sand," and, "Honey drips from the lips of a prostitute, which for a certain time is sweet to your palate. Afterwards you will find it more bitter than wormwood, sharper than a two-edged sword." Thus, eating it and enjoying it a little, afterwards he is devoured by worms, while he renders his soul far away, because the fool does not know that "they that are far from God perish."

"Those who do such things deserve to die." Which things? Those he had previously listed as punishments. In fact, "God gave them up," he says, "in the lusts of their hearts to impurity, because they do that which should not be done. To be an adulterer is already a kind of punishment; to be a liar, a miser, a cheat, a murderer, these are already punishments. Punishments for which sin? Of the primordial apostasy, the supreme sin of pride. "The beginning of human sin is rebellion against God," and, "The beginning of every sin is pride." For the apostle had spoken of this antecedent of sin: "Although they knew God, they neither gave him glory nor rendered thanks to him; instead, they have become futile in their reasonings, and their obtuse minds have become darkened." A darkened heart is already a punishment. But from what does it derive? "While declaring themselves wise, they have become…

"The gate of hell" means the beginning of sin because it is written, "The wages of sin is death," and to say "death" is equivalent to saying "hell." The Scripture also explains what constitutes the beginning of sin: "The beginning of every sin is pride." Therefore pride is the gate of hell. When one inquires concerning the causes that have produced heresies, one sees that they were born from pride because pride pushes people, in the end, toward heresies and schisms when they boast of their abilities and their holiness with the goal of attracting people to themselves but with the result of detaching them from Christ. But all heresies and schisms derive from these children of pride who will not overcome the catholic church, as it was precisely foretold, "The gates of hell will not prevail against it."
